F-15 publication-time shadowing boundary: alias uniqueness and physical-name shadowing are validated when a candidate successor Store MAP is being published, against the comparison domain applicable to that one Store snapshot and the then-visible governed physical targets it makes row-addressable. If an alias would exactly collide with another addressable alias or physical filename in that publication domain, publication refuses. After a Store MAP has been validly published, the later appearance, disappearance, rename, or copying-in of an unrelated Suitcase file does not retroactively make that immutable MAP structurally invalid or ineligible. A later textual reference can still become ambiguous at resolution time under W002-STOR-021; that ambiguity causes the later operation to refuse rather than changing the historical MAP's validity.

The store_alias names the Store as a whole and is separate from the field/COL alias namespace. Alias mutation occurs through a governed Work Order, not through an editable GUI field. Exact cross-Store Store-alias uniqueness and future selection-by-Store-alias syntax remain outside this freeze.

W002-STOR-021

Work Order resolution binds one exact Store MAP and physical targets

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A saved Work Order may refer to governed materialized columns by exact physical filename or by a unique COL alias from one selected Store MAP. The canonical explicit Store-MAP selector is MAP "<exact Store MAP filename>" under W002-STOR-019.3 and W002-WKO-012.3. If that clause is present and valid, exactly that Store snapshot is used. Otherwise Data Sculptor applies the Store-aware source-qualified selection rule in W002-STOR-019.2.

All textual physical-filename and COL-alias comparisons in this resolution step use exact Unicode scalar-value sequence equality under PB-STOR-010: no case folding, Unicode normalization, trimming, locale equivalence, or filesystem enumeration heuristic is permitted. Resolution is bounded to the selected Store snapshot and the physical targets/aliases that are addressable through that snapshot. If the supplied text has no exact target, resolution refuses. If it has more than one exact possible target in that domain—for example because a currently visible physical filename and a current alias are both exact matches—resolution also refuses. Data Sculptor must not choose filename over alias, alias over filename, first-found entry, directory order, modified time, UUID, or any other tie-break heuristic.

Before execution, Data Sculptor must record the exact physical Store MAP identity when one is used, bind the run to its exact rid_filename, and resolve aliases deterministically to physical COL artifacts. The selected Store MAP must remain fixed for the run even if a newer MAP is created during that same run. This protects Store/selection continuity but does not by itself claim that bytes stored under an analyst-owned source filename are cryptographically identical across different runs.

W002-STOR-022

Each successful Suitcase validation publishes one retained governed CER HTML certificate

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A selected directory becomes a validated Suitcase only when Data Sculptor successfully creates, completely writes, and closes one governed CER HTML Suitcase Validation Certificate in that directory. The certificate itself is the validation artifact and remains visible in the flat Suitcase as durable evidence.

No validation-only delete or rename is required. Failure to create, completely write, or close the certificate means the directory has not passed Suitcase validation and analytical execution remains locked.

F-14 CER exception: the CER is deliberately not staged as SCR. Suitcase validation is specifically the direct create/write/close test of the final canonical CER identity in the selected directory. Inserting an SCR-to-CER rename would test a different publication path and is therefore forbidden for this validation step. A successful CER does not pre-certify later SCR-to-final renames for other artifact classes.

F-24 CER lifecycle: every successful explicit Suitcase selection and validation publishes exactly one fresh immutable CER with a new governed UTC+UUID identity. Data Sculptor must not satisfy a new validation event by reusing an earlier CER. Every prior valid CER remains a standalone historical artifact under its original governed filename and exact bytes.

WASM-002 performs no automatic CER deletion, replacement, compaction, or CER-history ZIP packaging. Historical CERs are not housekeeping candidates merely because a newer CER exists. Any later archival or packaging capability must be separately governed and explicitly invoked; it is not part of the WASM-002 validation lifecycle.

W002-STOR-022.1

Suitcase Validation Certificate physical identity and longest-name path gate

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The exact certificate filename is __DS__CER__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.html, using the canonical UTC millisecond token and canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID v4. Data Sculptor chooses the filename; the analyst does not supply or edit it.

The CER create/write/close test begins only after the browser host has satisfied the required user-selected writable-directory capability in W002-PLAT-001. A browser that cannot expose that capability produces a host-capability refusal before folder validation; that condition is not evidence that any particular directory is unwritable or filename-incompatible.

WASM-002 path/filename acceptance must derive the maximum filename length from every governed final-artifact filename form and every governed SCR staging form that this build can actually emit. Under the current contract, the maximum is 73 ASCII bytes/characters: the governed .html CER/HLP final forms and an SCR candidate reserved for a .html final artifact have that length. The canonical CER filename therefore exercises the current maximum emitted filename length during the create/write/close validation test.

On a supported host, successful create/write/close of this canonical governed HTML filename is the WASM-002 folder filename/path compatibility test for the current emitted-name maximum. Data Sculptor does not maintain a product-level table of operating-system numeric path maxima and must not truncate, abbreviate, hash-shorten, or otherwise mutate a governed filename to fit a host path limitation. If the certificate cannot be created under its canonical name after a directory has actually been selected through the supported-host contract, the selected directory does not pass validation.

If a future PRD revision introduces an emitted final or staging filename longer than the current CER/HLP/SCR-HTML maximum, acceptance must detect that change and explicitly exercise the new maximum before the build may rely on this path-compatibility claim.

W002-STOR-022.2

Suitcase Validation Certificate semantic content

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The HTML certificate uses the canonical built-in Data Sculptor presentation and must visibly contain, at minimum:

SUITCASE VALIDATION CERTIFICATE
RESULT: PASS
SUITCASE: .
UTC: <canonical certificate UTC>
UUID: <certificate UUID>
ARTIFACT: <full governed certificate filename>
TEST: CREATE_WRITE_CLOSE

It must state that Data Sculptor successfully created, completely wrote, and closed this governed HTML certificate in the selected Suitcase. It must state that this establishes that the selected directory was writable by Data Sculptor at the recorded UTC and accepted the governed artifact filename used for the certificate.

It must also state that the certificate does not certify available disk capacity, guarantee success of future analytical operations, or certify later SCR-to-final-class publication/rename operations. The semantic record uses SUITCASE: . and must not persist an absolute machine-specific path merely to prove validation.

W002-STOR-022.3

Suitcase Validation Certificate uses the canonical built-in presentation in WASM-002

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The certificate is a human-facing HTML CER artifact and uses the canonical built-in Red5Sorcery/Data Sculptor presentation in WASM-002. Presentation must never change RESULT, SUITCASE, UTC, UUID, artifact identity, TEST, validation meaning, or limitation facts.

Configurable Brand Manifest application to CER artifacts is deferred to V1-BACKLOG / a future build and is not required for WASM-002 Suitcase validation.

W002-STOR-023

Non-Store governed artifacts use class-specific all-or-refuse publication profiles

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Except for the deliberate CER Suitcase-validation path below, WASM-002 does not place a newly generated durable artifact into its final semantic class merely because candidate bytes exist. The complete candidate is first written under the governed SCR identity defined by W002-STOR-023.1, closed, reopened, and validated against the target class contract. Only a candidate that passes its class-specific publication predicate may be renamed into the intended final class. A final-class filename therefore records successful class publication, not broader authority where a separate MAP/registry relationship governs authority.

F-33 reserved-class boundary: DGN, RCV, BRD, and LCK are registered but not emitted by WASM-002, so they do not appear as publication profiles in this table and have no WASM-002 producer here.

Final classFinal serialization / identityPublication predicateAuthority boundary
WKO__DS__WKO__<UTC>__<UUID>.txtThe complete candidate obeys the saved-Work-Order lifecycle and parses completely under exactly one WASM-002 executable operation grammar with the required SUITCASE: ., exactly one non-whitespace WORK ORDER AS alias, and the governed lexical/comment rules. Applicable save-time alias/registry gates must also pass before the save transaction may commit.Promotion proves a valid immutable WKO artifact. Alias-registry authority is not committed until the complete successor WKO MAP is successfully published under W002-STOR-018.3.

It does not retroactively create or change analytical state.

It does not override the underlying diagnostic event or analytical state.

Structural CSV interpretation remains a later certification/materialization concern.The published exact CVT filename is a new immutable governed source identity for later routing under W002-CONV-004.

No SCR staging/rename is inserted into this test.The CER proves that canonical governed create/write/close succeeded in the selected directory at that recorded moment. It does not pre-certify later SCR-to-final publication.

RID, COL, Store MAP and WKO MAP publication retain their specialized transaction/commit rules elsewhere in this PRD. W002-STOR-023 does not replace those state-publication contracts; W002-STOR-023.1 supplies the shared SCR candidate identity and retained-failure-evidence boundary they may reference.

W002-STOR-023.1

SCR candidates preserve intended final identity; retained failure evidence remains non-authoritative

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The canonical candidate filename for a staged governed artifact is:

__DS__SCR__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.<final-extension>

The SCR candidate uses the exact UTC token, UUID and extension reserved for its intended final artifact. Successful publication changes only the three-letter semantic class token from SCR to the intended final class. For example, an RCP candidate __DS__SCR__20261006T190000000Z__<uuid>.txt may become __DS__RCP__20261006T190000000Z__<uuid>.txt only after the complete candidate has been closed, reopened and validated against the RCP publication predicate. The rename must not alter candidate bytes, UTC, UUID or extension.

An SCR filename never by itself confers final-class validity, Store membership, registry authority, execution authority, or durable final-class evidence status. A retained SCR whose bytes happen to satisfy a target validator after an interrupted or refused transaction must not be auto-promoted, silently adopted, or treated as if the missing publication step occurred.

F-33 retained-failure-evidence boundary: when a handled failure leaves one or more SCR candidates or other staged bytes that cannot be safely removed or restored, they must remain visible only as non-authoritative SCR evidence. WASM-002 does not publish an RCV recovery manifest. Retention must not complete or simulate the failed publication step, and the governed diagnostic/Help path must report the failure using only facts actually established.

A retained or orphaned SCR remains non-authoritative even if its bytes later validate. Data Sculptor must not infer an intended final class solely from extension or byte content, must not rename or promote the SCR merely because it survives a later scan, and must not create a replacement RCV sidecar to manufacture attribution that the failed transaction did not durably preserve.

W002-ENC-001

Strict whole-file UTF-8 certification

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Before WASM-002 performs analytical CSV materialization, it must certify the complete selected source as valid UTF-8 using bounded processing.

W002-ENC-001.1

Certification must examine the entire source, not merely a prefix, sample, BOM, or first analytical window.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-001.2

UTF-8 validity must be determined across chunk boundaries, including incomplete multi-byte sequences that span adjacent input windows.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-001.3

A UTF-8 BOM, when present, is parsing metadata and must not be treated as proof that the remainder of the source is valid UTF-8.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-001.4

Certification must preserve exact source-byte accounting.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-001.5

Certification must operate within the governed WASM memory budget.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Stage 1 UTF-8 certification must remain bounded independently of source byte length and must not buffer the complete source, CSV header, or CSV row set in memory. CSV column-count and operational-name rules belong to Stage 2 and must not be used to justify unbounded Stage-1 state.

W002-ENC-001.6

Certification must produce deterministic PASS or FAIL for the same source bytes under the same frozen rules.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-002

UTF-8 certification is a hard analytical gate

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The WASM-002 analytical/materialization path must proceed only after successful UTF-8 certification.

W002-ENC-002.1

If UTF-8 certification fails, the current analytical Work Order must stop.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-002.2

The analytical engine must not silently switch to another decoder.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-002.3

The analytical engine must not continue materialization under an inferred or guessed source encoding.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-002.4

No Windows-1252 transcoding may occur as an implicit sub-step of the failed analytical Work Order.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-003

Certification and materialization share one run-local selected source

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

For a governed WASM-002 analytical run, the browser host must resolve the Work Order source reference once and retain the same selected source instance across Stage 1 UTF-8 certification and Stage 2 materialization.

The purpose of this binding is to prevent Stage 2 from accidentally consuming a different source than the one Stage 1 certified. It is a run-local continuity guarantee, not a claim of durable cryptographic identity across separate runs.

W002-ENC-003.1

Stage 2 must not re-resolve or substitute the source

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

After Stage 1 begins, Stage 2 must not reacquire the analytical source by re-reading an alias mapping, re-resolving a filename/path, opening a newly selected browser file, or otherwise substituting another source instance. Stage 2 consumes the source instance already bound to the governed run.

W002-ENC-003.2

Filename, alias, path, or byte length alone is not durable byte identity

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Filename equality, alias equality, path equality, timestamps, or exact byte length may be useful provenance facts but must not be presented as cryptographic proof that source bytes are identical across separate runs. WASM-002 makes no such automatic cross-run exact-byte claim.

W002-ENC-003.3

Ordinary WASM-002 source binding does not require automatic SHA-256

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

UTF-8 certification and ordinary column materialization must not automatically compute SHA-256 merely to establish WASM-002 source binding. The source-binding requirement is satisfied by preserving the same run-local selected source instance across the two stages.

This rule does not prohibit SHA-256 where another explicit WASM-002 requirement governs integrity for a specific generated artifact. It applies to automatic hashing of ordinary analytical source data.

W002-ENC-003.4

Loss of run-local source continuity causes refusal

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

If the browser host cannot preserve the selected source instance from certification into materialization, or the source becomes unavailable before Stage 2 can consume it, the analytical run must refuse before materialization rather than silently reselect, substitute, or infer another source.

W002-ENC-004

ASCII-first inline UTF-8 certification algorithm

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

WASM-002 must use an ASCII-first, strict inline UTF-8 certification algorithm or an equivalent implementation that preserves the same single-forward-scan semantics, bounded state, deterministic validity result, exact error location, and performance intent established by WASM-001b.

W002-ENC-004.1

The certifier must process the source in bounded windows and must not allocate memory proportional to source-file size.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-004.2

The 4 MiB window used in WASM-001b is a proven reference point, not a frozen WASM-002 production constant.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Window size may be changed only if semantics and byte-identical certification outcomes remain invariant.

W002-ENC-004.3

At the beginning of each window, any incomplete UTF-8 sequence carried from the preceding window must be resolved before the remaining bytes are treated as independent input.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-004.4

When there is no pending cross-window sequence, consecutive bytes below 0x80 must be recognized as ASCII and certified directly because ASCII is a complete subset of UTF-8.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-004.5

An all-ASCII window with no pending cross-window sequence must be certifiable without submitting the same bytes to a second general UTF-8 decoder pass.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-004.6

When a byte at or above 0x80 is encountered, the certifier must validate the UTF-8 sequence inline, then resume the ASCII-fast scan after the valid sequence.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-004.7

The implementation must not require collecting all non-ASCII bytes, all non-ASCII runs, or all non-ASCII offsets for later validation.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-004.8

The implementation must not require a separate general-purpose string-decoder call for each non-ASCII sequence.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

An equivalent low-overhead strict validator is acceptable if it preserves the same governed result and bounded-state behavior.

W002-ENC-004.9

Cross-window state must be bounded to the information required for at most one incomplete UTF-8 sequence.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

No more than three source bytes may need to remain pending between windows, or an equivalent smaller state representation may be used.

W002-ENC-004.10

On the first invalid UTF-8 sequence, certification must stop and report the exact absolute source-byte offset required by the frozen error contract.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

On the first invalid UTF-8 sequence, certification must stop and return FAIL. The governed UTF-8 refusal evidence is:

  • FIRST_INVALID_BYTE_OFFSET — the zero-based absolute byte offset of the first byte of the invalid sequence, counted from the first physical source byte, including a permitted leading UTF-8 BOM when present; and
  • STOP_REASON — exactly INVALID_UTF8_SEQUENCE.

For an EOF-truncated multibyte sequence, FIRST_INVALID_BYTE_OFFSET is the absolute offset of that incomplete sequence's lead byte, not the EOF position. The certifier need not read the remainder of an already-invalid source. Input-window boundaries must not change the outcome, stop reason, or first-invalid offset.

F-16 follow-on boundary: stopping strict UTF-8 certification at the first invalid sequence does not make the remainder of the source irrelevant to conversion advice. When the governing operation is MATERIALIZE and Stage 1 reaches FAIL, the analytical run remains refused; Data Sculptor then starts the separate read-only compatibility assessment in W002-CONV-002 from physical byte offset 0 of the same bound source instance. That second pass may read to EOF solely to determine converter compatibility. Stage 2 must not start.

W002-ENC-004.11

At EOF, certification may return PASS only if every source byte has been consumed under the strict UTF-8 rules and no incomplete sequence remains pending.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

At EOF, certification may return PASS only if every physical source byte has been consumed under the strict UTF-8 rules and no incomplete sequence remains pending.

The completed Stage-1 outcome vocabulary is exactly PASS and FAIL. PASS means strict whole-source UTF-8 certification completed successfully. FAIL means an invalid UTF-8 sequence was deterministically established under W002-ENC-004.10.

The common Receipt absence tokens remain separate from those completed outcomes: NOT_RUN when Stage 1 never begins, and NOT_AVAILABLE when Stage 1 begins but a separate failure prevents a governed PASS/FAIL conclusion. NOT_APPLICABLE is not a completed value for STAGE1_UTF8_OUTCOME.

W002-ENC-004.12

A UTF-8 BOM at absolute source offset zero may be recognized as BOM metadata after its bytes are validated, but the remaining source must still undergo complete certification.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-004.13

The certifier must not perform CSV delimiter, quote, header, row, or analytical interpretation.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Certification answers only whether the complete source byte stream is valid UTF-8 under the frozen rules.

W002-ENC-004.14

Certification results must be independent of window boundaries.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Splitting the same valid or invalid source at different bounded window sizes must not change PASS/FAIL or the first invalid absolute byte offset.

W002-ENC-004.15

The certifier must expose enough measured counters for acceptance evidence to reconcile source bytes read, windows/pushes processed, non-ASCII sequences encountered when counted, final pending state, and stop reason without requiring those counters to alter certification semantics.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-005

Strict UTF-8 byte-sequence rules

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The inline validator must implement strict modern UTF-8 validity, excluding overlong forms, UTF-16 surrogate code points, values above U+10FFFF, invalid lead bytes, invalid continuation bytes, and truncated sequences.

F-07 stop-reason vocabulary: all strict UTF-8 invalidity classes governed by this requirement—lone continuation bytes, malformed continuation sequences, overlong forms, surrogate encodings, values above U+10FFFF, invalid lead bytes, and EOF-truncated sequences—serialize the single machine reason token INVALID_UTF8_SEQUENCE. The specific fixture category is acceptance evidence; the canonical stop reason intentionally does not duplicate validator-library-specific subcodes.

W002-ENC-005.1

Single-byte ASCII is 0x00 through 0x7F.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-005.2

Two-byte sequences must begin with 0xC2 through 0xDF and be followed by exactly one continuation byte 0x80 through 0xBF.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-005.3

Three-byte sequences beginning with 0xE0 must use a second byte 0xA0 through 0xBF and a third byte 0x80 through 0xBF, preventing overlong encodings.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-005.4

Three-byte sequences beginning with 0xE1 through 0xEC or 0xEE through 0xEF must use two continuation bytes 0x80 through 0xBF.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-005.5

Three-byte sequences beginning with 0xED must use a second byte 0x80 through 0x9F and a third byte 0x80 through 0xBF, excluding UTF-16 surrogate halves.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-005.6

Four-byte sequences beginning with 0xF0 must use a second byte 0x90 through 0xBF followed by two continuation bytes 0x80 through 0xBF, preventing overlong encodings.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-005.7

Four-byte sequences beginning with 0xF1 through 0xF3 must use three continuation bytes 0x80 through 0xBF.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-005.8

Four-byte sequences beginning with 0xF4 must use a second byte 0x80 through 0x8F followed by two continuation bytes 0x80 through 0xBF, preventing code points above U+10FFFF.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-005.9

Bytes 0x80 through 0xBF are invalid when encountered as lead bytes.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-005.10

Bytes 0xC0 and 0xC1 are invalid lead bytes because they can only introduce overlong encodings.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-ENC-005.11

Bytes 0xF5 through 0xFF are invalid UTF-8 lead bytes.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Figure 2. The WASM-001b-derived fast path certifies ASCII directly, validates only non-ASCII sequences inline, and carries only bounded state across windows.

W002-ENC-006

Measured evidence inherited from WASM-001b

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The following measurements are non-normative evidence explaining why WASM-002 begins with the ASCII-first inline algorithm. They are not WASM-002 acceptance results and must not be represented as such.

EVID-W001B-UTF8-001 On the 7,250,808,204-byte Statistics Canada source, the Day 039 distribution experiment observed 659,103 non-ASCII bytes, approximately 0.009090063% of the file, across 329,551 non-ASCII runs/sequences; the maximum observed non-ASCII run was three bytes.

EVID-W001B-UTF8-002 The Day 039 non-ASCII-only experiment submitted only 659,103 bytes to strict UTF-8 validation and completed in 12.664716 seconds at 545.998 MiB/s; it proved the source valid but still incurred 329,551 strict validation calls.

EVID-W001B-UTF8-003 A 1 GiB A/B test showed that reducing validated bytes alone was not enough: the selective per-run strategy submitted 115,839 bytes in 57,919 strict calls but took 503.7536 ms, while the baseline submitted 113,246,208 bytes in 27 strict calls and took 411.3590 ms.

UNRESOLVED SOURCE DAMAGE: preserved authoritative text continues “This supported removing per-run general-validator call overhead rather than merely shrinking” but the remainder has not been recovered. No missing words are inferred or supplied.

EVID-W001B-UTF8-004 The final native inline scan certified all 7,250,808,204 bytes in 10.377870 seconds at 666.313 MiB/s, observed 329,551 non-ASCII sequences and 659,103 non-ASCII bytes, and made zero std::str::from_utf8 calls.

EVID-W001B-UTF8-005 The same inline design was exercised in Microsoft Edge/WASM with 4 MiB transfers: the valid 7,250,808,204-byte source completed with 1,729 pushes, UTF8_VALID=true, and EOF_ALL_BYTES_VALID. That experimental run took 30.5858 seconds including file I/O, JS-to-WASM copy, and WASM validation.

EVID-W001B-UTF8-006 A full-size deliberately invalid Edge/WASM fixture stopped early after 2,936,012,800 bytes and 700 pushes with UTF8_VALID=false and STOP_REASON=INVALID_UTF8_SEQUENCE rather than reading to EOF.

EVID-W001B-UTF8-007 WASM-001b also retained malformed UTF-8 fixtures for stray legacy bytes, truncated sequences, lone continuation bytes, overlong encodings, UTF-16 surrogate halves, and 0xFE/0xFF invalid bytes. WASM-002 should reuse or regenerate equivalent acceptance fixtures with known invalid offsets.

W002-MAT-001

Stage 2 consumes the source instance certified by Stage 1

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The structural CSV parser and materializer operate under the explicit invariant that the same run-local selected source instance has already passed governed whole-file UTF-8 certification. Stage 2 must not independently re-resolve the analytical source.

Stage 1 establishes encoding validity. Stage 2 establishes CSV structure, row identity, selected values, and governed outputs.

W002-MAT-001.1

Stage 2 must not independently re-decide the source encoding.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-MAT-001.2

Stage 2 must not contain an automatic Windows-1252 fallback.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-MAT-001.3

Stage 2 may perform only those byte/character checks required for correct CSV structural parsing and frozen analytical semantics.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-MAT-001.4

Any implementation shortcut that would weaken the certified-source invariant must be treated as a PRD change, not an optimization.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-MAT-001.5

Stage 2 restarts at byte offset zero of the same certified source instance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

After Stage 1 returns PASS, Stage 2 must begin its structural pass from absolute source byte offset zero using the same run-local selected source instance. Rewinding/re-reading the existing source handle is permitted; performing a new filename, alias, path, picker, or directory resolution is not.

If the host cannot re-read that same selected source instance for Stage 2, the Work Order must refuse under the run-local source-continuity contract.

W002-MAT-001.6

Stage 2 consumes an offset-zero UTF-8 BOM as metadata before header parsing

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

If the certified source begins with the UTF-8 BOM bytes EF BB BF, Stage 2 must consume those three bytes before parsing the first CSV header field. They must not become part of the first source header or selected value.

The BOM is recognized only at absolute source offset zero. The fact that Stage 1 already saw the BOM does not permit Stage 2 to skip or reinterpret arbitrary later bytes.

W002-MAT-001.7

Stage 2 parses the header once and then continues directly into the data-record scan

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Within the Stage 2 forward source scan, Data Sculptor must parse the complete first logical CSV record as the source header, construct ordered header metadata including exact decoded header text and 1-based source ordinal, resolve and validate all Work Order selectors/aliases, and then continue from the first data record without restarting the source.

Header resolution therefore does not add a third whole-file pass. A header-only valid CSV yields a zero-row materialization; a source with no valid header record refuses.

P3-09 no-header-record refusal: after Stage 1 has certified the source, if Stage 2 reaches end-of-source without establishing any logical CSV record from which a header could be parsed, materialization must refuse with CSV_REFUSAL_CONDITION: NO_HEADER_RECORD. This is the eighth governed Stage-2 structural CSV refusal token in the canonical oracle defined by W002-MAT-002.8. Its governed location facts are: CSV_SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET = exact source byte length; CSV_PHYSICAL_LINE: 1; CSV_LOGICAL_RECORD: 1; CSV_FIELD_ORDINAL: 1. Therefore a zero-byte source reports offset 0, and a source containing only the UTF-8 BOM bytes EF BB BF reports offset 3. A first logical record that exists but is blank remains governed by the already-frozen BLANK_LOGICAL_RECORD condition and must not be reclassified as NO_HEADER_RECORD.

F-20 source-width boundary: the established header record may contain at most 16,384 physical source columns. Exactly 16,384 is valid; a header record containing 16,385 or more fields must refuse deterministically during header resolution before the first data record is consumed. The bound applies to the complete physical source width, not merely the requested KEEP set.

Header processing must remain bounded. Exact decoded source-header text is authoritative source evidence and must be preserved for every selected/materialized column, but the implementation is not required to retain the complete decoded text of every unselected header after selector resolution when bounded metadata is sufficient.

W002-MAT-001.8

Stage 2 relies on Stage 1 UTF-8 validity rather than revalidating the file

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Stage 2 must not run a second whole-file UTF-8 certification algorithm over the source. It may inspect bytes and decoded field content only as required for CSV structure, header/selector semantics, governed field-size limits, output serialization, and diagnostics.

Any implementation that reintroduces redundant whole-source UTF-8 validation into Stage 2 is a measurable architectural regression unless separately justified and accepted.

W002-MAT-002

One-pass multi-column materialization

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A valid Work Order may request multiple source columns for materialization during the same bounded structural pass. For WASM-002 DS-STEPS, the requested set is expressed by one KEEP block containing one or more HEADER and/or COLUMN selectors under W002-STEPS-001 through W002-STEPS-004.

F-20 KEEP-width boundary: one governed KEEP block may resolve from 1 through 16,384 distinct source columns, subject to the source itself containing no more than 16,384 columns. An empty KEEP or a request that cannot resolve within that bound refuses before data-row materialization.

W002-MAT-002.1

Requested columns must be resolved and validated before data-row materialization begins

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Every HEADER and COLUMN selector in the governed KEEP block must resolve to exactly one source column before any data-row materialization begins. Missing headers, ambiguous duplicate-header matches, invalid/out-of-range ordinals, duplicate resolved selections, invalid aliases, and successor-MAP alias collisions must refuse before the structural data-row pass.

The resolved selection cardinality must be an integer from 1 through 16,384. Resolution/validation must finish before the first data record is consumed, including operational-name/default-alias derivation and any deterministic oversized-header fallback required by W002-STOR-019.7.

W002-MAT-002.2

All selected columns are emitted from one forward data-record scan

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

After header/selector resolution, Stage 2 must traverse the source data records once regardless of whether the Work Order selects one column or many. The engine must not perform one complete source rescan per requested column.

During that scan, every source field is interpreted structurally, but only the fields required by the resolved selection set are materialized into governed COL outputs.

F-20 one-pass boundary: “one forward data-record scan” means one traversal of the source data records for the MATERIALIZE operation. WASM-002 must not reread source data records in batches merely because the selected-column set is wide. An implementation may perform additional bounded passes over Data-Sculptor-owned SCR, spool, or staging structures after the source scan when needed to finalize many outputs within resource limits; such passes must not reread the source data records or change governed output semantics.

W002-MAT-002.3

One 1-based logical row ordinal aligns every selected output

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The header is not a data row. The first accepted logical data record is row identity 1, the next is 2, and so on through N. The row counter advances exactly once per accepted logical CSV data record, not per physical line. Every selected COL produced by the run must contain exactly one logical data record for each accepted source data row and therefore exactly N data records in the same governed order. A multiline quoted field remains part of one logical record and must not advance row identity merely because it contains physical newline bytes.

When the run establishes a new Store, this 1..N sequence is published as that Store's one governed RID artifact. When the run extends an existing Store without changing its row universe, the existing RID is reused and must not be regenerated or renumbered.

W002-MAT-002.4

Selected-column writer order follows resolved KEEP order

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Before the data-record scan begins, the validated selection set is placed in the same order in which its selectors appear in the governed KEEP block. That resolved order governs writer creation, per-row selected-field dispatch, progress/receipt presentation, deterministic backpressure-drain priority, and candidate COL identity allocation.

The Store MAP's own CSV mapping-row ordering remains governed separately by W002-STOR-019.9 and must not be confused with Work Order selection order.

W002-MAT-002.5

Multiple active COL outputs use bounded staging and explicit backpressure

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Each active materialized-column writer, or an equivalent shared multiplexed output structure, must have bounded staging capacity. The aggregate kernel-owned staging state for all active writers must remain inside the governed WASM memory budget and must not grow with source row count or total output size.

If a required output writer cannot accept additional canonical bytes without exceeding its governed staging capacity, source consumption must pause while pending output is drained/written. When more than one writer requires service, drain priority follows resolved KEEP order. After sufficient space is available, parsing resumes from the same structural state.

The exact tuned staging-buffer size is an implementation/benchmark constant rather than an analytical semantic constant; changing it must not change output bytes, row identity, selection results, or diagnostics for the same governed input.

F-20 writer-resource bound: KEEP width and simultaneously active writable resources are distinct. The accepted build must declare a finite implementation bound on simultaneously active writable-output resources and retain acceptance evidence of both that configured bound and the observed peak. The engine may satisfy a wide selection by bounded shared/multiplexed staging or a Data-Sculptor-owned spool followed by bounded finalization passes, but it must not require one simultaneously open writer per selected column. Changing the writer-resource bound must not change final bytes, row order, selection identity, aliases, Receipts, or diagnostics for the same governed input.

W002-MAT-002.6

Partial output sets are never published as a successful materialization

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

All requested materialized-column outputs begin as visible governed SCR candidates, not COL artifacts. On first materialization of a new Store, the automatically generated RID likewise begins as a governed SCR candidate. Before any new RID/COL SCR candidate is opened, Data Sculptor establishes one publication-transaction UTC under PB-STOR-013/PB-STOR-014 and allocates a distinct artifact-specific UUID for each new candidate. Each candidate filename therefore already carries the exact UTC, UUID, and final extension intended for that RID or COL identity. A materialization transaction may begin promotion only when every required RID/COL candidate reaches EOF successfully, all selected outputs reconcile to the same accepted data-row count N, and all required candidate finalization/validation succeeds.

F-04 existing-Store cardinality gate: when materialization targets an existing VALID Store, after Stage 2 establishes the complete candidate logical data-row count N and before any requested COL candidate is promoted, Data Sculptor must read the expected N from the already-valid inherited RID header and compare the two values. If candidate N equals RID-header N, the cardinality gate passes and ordinary publication may continue. If candidate N differs, the Run must refuse before any SCR-to-COL promotion and before successor-MAP publication. The inherited RID, current MAP, and existing COL artifacts remain unchanged, and the existing Store remains VALID. Equal N proves cardinality compatibility only; it does not prove source-byte continuity, row-semantic identity, or permission for a different SOURCE to enter the lineage. Exact SOURCE/Store compatibility rules are prior gates.

For a new Store, Data Sculptor promotes the validated RID candidate first by host rename that changes only the class token from SCR to RID; the candidate bytes, shared transaction UTC, RID-specific UUID, and extension remain unchanged. That successful SCR-to-RID promotion is the event that establishes RID_ACTION: CREATED and the published RID_FILENAME fact for the Run. Before that promotion succeeds, the Run has not created a governed RID even if a candidate identity has been allocated.

For an existing Store, the inherited RID is reused unchanged and no RID candidate/promotion occurs. Once routing has selected and validated that exact inherited RID, that event establishes RID_ACTION: REUSED and the exact inherited RID_FILENAME; later refusal does not erase the already-established reuse fact. After the required RID state is established, Data Sculptor promotes each requested COL candidate in deterministic resolved KEEP order by changing only the class token from SCR to COL; each candidate's bytes, shared transaction UTC, COL-specific UUID, and extension remain unchanged.

If RID or COL promotion fails, Data Sculptor must refuse the run and roll any newly promoted RID/COL names back out of their final namespaces where safely possible. Candidate or rollback bytes that cannot be safely restored or removed must be retained visibly as non-authoritative SCR failure evidence. The existence of an unreferenced RID- or COL-looking file after interruption does not by itself make that artifact committed Store state.

After all required RID/COL promotions succeed, Data Sculptor allocates a MAP-specific UUID before opening the complete successor-MAP SCR candidate. That candidate uses the same publication-transaction UTC, the allocated MAP UUID, and the final .csv extension, and is constructed using the exact final RID/COL filenames. It is closed successfully, reopened, and validated completely while it remains SCR. Only then may the MAP candidate be promoted by changing only the class token from SCR to MAP; its bytes, UTC, UUID, and extension remain unchanged. The successful SCR-to-MAP rename is the materialization commit point.

Until that commit point, the prior valid MAP remains authoritative for an existing Store; for a new Store, no committed Store state exists yet. If MAP validation or MAP rename fails, Data Sculptor must refuse and roll the newly promoted RID/COL set back out of the final namespaces where safely possible; otherwise affected bytes remain attributable recovery evidence and are not committed Store membership. Governed Store membership/current state is established by a valid MAP binding, not by a final-class filename or timestamp equality alone.

Revision BB preserves the Revision AY staging/promotion mechanics and Revision AZ shared transaction-UTC rule for newly published RID/COL/MAP artifacts. Selected-folder support for the canonical governed filename/path form is established by the Suitcase Validation Certificate under W002-STOR-022 through W002-STOR-022.3 rather than by a frozen numeric host path-length table. Operation-specific host rename or publication failure remains a governed refusal under this requirement and is not pre-certified by Suitcase validation.

F-14 shared candidate grammar, reconciled by F-33: every RID/COL/MAP SCR candidate in this transaction follows W002-STOR-023.1: its SCR name already carries the UTC, UUID and extension intended for the final RID/COL/MAP identity, and successful promotion changes only the class token. Any retained SCR candidates after a handled publication/rollback failure remain visible non-authoritative failure evidence under W002-STOR-023.1 and are reported through the governed diagnostic/Help path; WASM-002 does not emit an RCV manifest. An orphaned SCR remains non-authoritative even if its bytes later validate.

W002-MAT-002.7

Successful materialization publishes one complete Store MAP

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A successful governed materialization that creates one or more COL artifacts must also publish exactly one new complete immutable Store MAP under W002-STOR-019 through W002-STOR-019.12. For a new Store, that MAP binds the automatically generated and promoted RID to the Store metadata and all newly materialized COL mappings. For an existing Store, it preserves the inherited RID binding and complete prior Store state while applying the successful materialization updates.

All required RID/COL SCR candidates must complete and validate before promotion begins. On a new Store, RID promotion occurs first; on an existing Store, the inherited RID is reused unchanged. All requested COL promotions must then succeed before successor-MAP candidate construction begins.

The complete successor MAP is written as SCR, closed, reopened, and fully validated before entering the MAP namespace. Its final host rename from SCR to the governed MAP filename occurs last and is the materialization commit point.

The materialization run is not reported as successfully committed until that MAP rename succeeds. If MAP candidate validation or MAP rename fails after RID/COL promotion, the run must refuse and the newly promoted artifacts must be rolled back out of their final namespaces where safely possible. Any failure residue that cannot safely be removed or restored is governed by W002-STOR-023.1 and remains non-authoritative retained failure evidence; its survival must not be used to infer or manufacture attribution or to simulate the failed publication step. The prior valid MAP remains authoritative for an existing Store; no committed Store is established for a first materialization without a valid successor MAP.

W002-MAT-002.8

Stage 2 enforces deterministic source-record shape

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The parsed header establishes the expected source field count. Every nonblank logical data record must contain exactly that many fields after CSV parsing. A nonblank ragged record with fewer or more fields must refuse rather than pad, truncate, or shift later values.

An explicit empty field is valid data and preserves its ordinal. A bare blank logical data record occurring outside a quoted field must refuse and must not be silently skipped or converted into one empty field. A physical blank line inside a valid quoted multiline field is field content, not a blank record.

F-06 canonical malformed-CSV refusal facts

Every structural CSV refusal records these governed facts:

REFUSAL_CONDITION
SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET
PHYSICAL_LINE
LOGICAL_RECORD
FIELD_ORDINAL
  • SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET is the zero-based absolute byte offset from the first physical byte of the source file. A leading UTF-8 BOM, when present, occupies offsets 0–2 and therefore counts in subsequent absolute byte locations.
  • PHYSICAL_LINE is one-based and equals one plus the number of LF bytes strictly before the governed refusal location. LF bytes inside quoted multiline fields still increment physical-line count.
  • LOGICAL_RECORD is one-based CSV logical-record ordinal and includes the header as logical record 1. The first data record is therefore logical record 2.
  • FIELD_ORDINAL is the one-based field position within that logical record.

These facts describe the same first structural refusal regardless of permitted streaming-window size or boundary placement.

Canonical structural refusal tokens

The seven frozen F-06 malformed-CSV tokens are:

UNEXPECTED_QUOTE_IN_UNQUOTED_FIELD
INVALID_BYTE_AFTER_CLOSING_QUOTE
BARE_CR_OUTSIDE_QUOTED_FIELD
EOF_INSIDE_QUOTED_FIELD
BLANK_LOGICAL_RECORD
TOO_FEW_FIELDS
TOO_MANY_FIELDS

P3-09 adds NO_HEADER_RECORD as the eighth governed Stage-2 structural CSV refusal token. Parser-library names, host exceptions, crate-specific error enums, or localized descriptions must not replace these governed tokens.

Governed refusal location by condition

ConditionGoverned refusal location
UNEXPECTED_QUOTE_IN_UNQUOTED_FIELDOffset of the offending " byte.
INVALID_BYTE_AFTER_CLOSING_QUOTEOffset of the first prohibited byte after the closing quote.
BARE_CR_OUTSIDE_QUOTED_FIELDOffset of the CR byte itself.
EOF_INSIDE_QUOTED_FIELDOne-past-end offset, equal to the physical source byte length.
BLANK_LOGICAL_RECORDFirst byte of the record terminator that proves the blank record: LF for LF termination; CR for CRLF termination.
TOO_FEW_FIELDSFirst byte of the record terminator that closes the short record; at EOF, one-past-end offset equal to source byte length.
TOO_MANY_FIELDSThe comma delimiter that begins the first field beyond the expected header width.
NO_HEADER_RECORDOne-past-end offset equal to the exact physical source byte length, with physical line 1, logical record 1, and field ordinal 1, as frozen by W002-MAT-001.7.

Field ordinal rules

  • For TOO_FEW_FIELDS, FIELD_ORDINAL is the first missing field ordinal: expected-width position immediately after the last field actually present.
  • For TOO_MANY_FIELDS, FIELD_ORDINAL is the first extra field ordinal: header-width + 1.
  • For quote/CR/EOF structural conditions, FIELD_ORDINAL is the current field ordinal in which the malformed condition is established.
  • For BLANK_LOGICAL_RECORD, FIELD_ORDINAL is 1.
  • For NO_HEADER_RECORD, FIELD_ORDINAL is 1.

Bare CR scope

A bare CR outside a quoted field is malformed CSV and refuses with BARE_CR_OUTSIDE_QUOTED_FIELD.

  • CR inside a valid quoted field is ordinary field content.
  • LF inside a valid quoted field is ordinary field content.
  • CRLF inside a valid quoted field is ordinary field content.
  • Outside quoted fields, CRLF is one accepted logical-record terminator and LF is one accepted logical-record terminator.
  • Outside quoted fields, a CR not immediately followed by LF is malformed.

EOF while quoted

If EOF is reached while the parser remains inside an open quoted field, the source refuses with EOF_INSIDE_QUOTED_FIELD.

Data Sculptor must not synthesize a closing quote, truncate the field, reinterpret prior bytes as unquoted content, or otherwise repair the source.

First-condition precedence

Stage 2 evaluates structural CSV input in absolute source-byte order and reports the earliest refusal condition that becomes deterministically established.

  • CSV grammar errors take precedence over later row-shape errors.
  • BLANK_LOGICAL_RECORD takes precedence over TOO_FEW_FIELDS for a physically blank logical record.
  • BARE_CR_OUTSIDE_QUOTED_FIELD takes precedence over INVALID_BYTE_AFTER_CLOSING_QUOTE when the post-quote offending byte is a CR that is not followed by LF.
  • At EOF while still inside a quoted field, EOF_INSIDE_QUOTED_FIELD takes precedence over field-count evaluation.

No implementation may choose a different error merely because of parser buffering, window boundaries, library behavior, or host platform.

Delimiter boundary

Comma remains the only WASM-002 field delimiter. Automatic delimiter detection is outside the WASM-002 CSV contract.

A file whose rows contain semicolons, tabs, or other non-comma separators may still be valid under the comma-only grammar as a one-column CSV. Data Sculptor must not invent a malformed-CSV refusal merely because another application would treat those bytes as delimiters.

When a requested HEADER cannot be resolved, Help may explain that WASM-002 uses comma as the CSV delimiter and that semicolon/tab exports may therefore be interpreted as one field per row.

Interaction with UTF-8 diagnostics

This structural CSV refusal oracle applies only after the source has passed the applicable encoding-certification boundary.

Invalid UTF-8 remains governed by the separately frozen UTF-8 diagnostic contract. Its zero-based absolute source-byte orientation is intentionally aligned with SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET so WASM-002 does not have competing byte-coordinate systems.

W002-MAT-002.9

Unselected field contents are not retained

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Stage 2 must parse every field sufficiently to preserve CSV structure, field count, row boundaries, and governed safety checks, but it must not retain complete contents for unselected fields after those bytes are no longer structurally needed.

The engine must not materialize a complete source row, complete table, or complete unselected column in memory merely to emit selected columns. Selected-field content may use bounded accumulation required by the frozen field-size/output rules.

W002-MAT-002.10

Individual decoded CSV fields are limited to 16 MiB

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

WASM-002 carries forward the established Data Sculptor field-buffer safety boundary: an individual CSV field may contain at most 16 MiB (16,777,216 bytes) of decoded UTF-8 field content. This is an engineering safety limit, not a semantic statement about CSV or an Excel cell limit.

The limit must be enforced incrementally for header and data fields. The parser must not first accumulate an arbitrarily large field and then check it. If a field would exceed the limit, the run must refuse without truncating, repairing, discarding the remainder, or finalizing the candidate materialization.

For an unselected field, Data Sculptor may count decoded field bytes without retaining the field value; the safety limit still applies so malformed unterminated fields cannot turn the structural scan into unbounded growth.

F-20 operational column-name boundary: after an exact source header field is decoded, Data Sculptor measures its length in Unicode scalar values, not UTF-8 bytes or grapheme clusters. If the exact decoded source header contains at most 1,024 Unicode scalar values, its operational column name is that exact header text. If it contains more than 1,024 scalar values, the operational column name begins from the deterministic physical-ordinal fallback Column <LETTERS>, where the letters are the Excel-style 1-based source ordinal (A through XFD for the WASM-002 width bound). This operational name is a bounded human-facing/default-alias construct; it does not replace or truncate the authoritative exact source header.

W002-MAT-002.11

Materialized COL artifacts use canonical one-column UTF-8 CSV serialization

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Each finalized materialized COL artifact is a one-column CSV. It begins with exactly one UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF) and uses LF (0x0A) as the record terminator on every supported host.

The first logical record contains the exact decoded source header text for that physical source column; an alias assigned with AS lives in the governed MAP and does not rewrite the physical COL header. A deliberately empty source header is serialized as one explicit empty header field rather than as absence of a header record.

Header and data fields use deterministic minimal CSV quoting: quote when the field contains comma, double quote, CR, or LF; double embedded double quotes; otherwise write the field without quotes. Embedded CR/LF that belong to a quoted field remain field content. For a one-column data record whose decoded value is the empty string, serialize the value explicitly as "" so the row cannot be confused with a bare blank logical record.

For fixed source bytes and fixed governed semantics, changing input/output window boundaries must not change the finalized COL bytes.

F-20 source-fidelity rule: the physical COL header record always serializes the exact decoded source header, even when that header exceeds the 1,024-scalar operational-name boundary and the Store MAP/default alias therefore uses an operational fallback. The fallback name must never be substituted into the COL header record or into the MAP source_header field.

W002-MAT-003

Stage 2 processes the source through bounded reusable windows

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Structural materialization must process the certified source through bounded reusable input windows compatible with browser/WASM memory constraints. Source size and row count must not require proportional WASM memory growth.

W002-MAT-003.1

The 4 MiB WASM-001b window is a proven reference point, not a frozen production constant

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The 4 MiB source window used successfully during the WASM-001b browser experiments is an evidence-backed starting/reference size. WASM-002 may tune the production input-window size using benchmark evidence, provided the governed memory budget and all window-invariance requirements remain satisfied.

W002-MAT-003.2

Changing source-window size or boundary placement must not change results

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

For the same certified source and Work Order, permitted changes in bounded Stage 2 input-window size or boundary placement must not change CSV interpretation, resolved headers/ordinals, accepted row count, row identity, aliases, canonical COL bytes, successor MAP contents apart from newly allocated physical identities/timestamps, or the first deterministic refusal condition.

P3-09 window invariance: for a Stage-1-certified source containing no logical CSV record, every permitted Stage 2 window size and boundary placement must produce the same NO_HEADER_RECORD refusal and the same governed location tuple: source-byte offset equal to the exact source byte length, physical line 1, logical record 1, field ordinal 1.

F-06 full refusal-oracle window invariance: for the same certified source bytes, changing any permitted Stage 2 input-window size or boundary placement must not change whether the source is accepted or refused; the first REFUSAL_CONDITION; SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET; PHYSICAL_LINE; LOGICAL_RECORD; or FIELD_ORDINAL. This applies to every structural CSV refusal governed by W002-MAT-002.8.

W002-MAT-003.3

CSV structure must survive arbitrary input-window boundaries

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Input-window boundaries may occur between ordinary field bytes, delimiter bytes, quote/escaped-quote pairs, CR/LF record-ending bytes, inside quoted multiline fields, and inside already-certified multi-byte UTF-8 sequences. The Stage 2 parser must preserve equivalent structural meaning across those boundaries.

W002-MAT-003.4

Cross-window parser state is small and explicit

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Stage 2 may carry only the bounded state needed to continue the current logical CSV parse, including the current logical row ordinal, current field ordinal, quoted/unquoted state, escaped-quote/quote-transition state as required by the parser, pending CR/LF state, decoded-field byte count, resolved selected-field dispatch metadata, and bounded selected-field/output staging.

The parser must not retain previous complete rows or source windows merely because a CSV record crosses a window boundary.

W002-MAT-003.5

Input-window and output-drain sizes are independent implementation controls

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The source read window, WASM transfer window where applicable, selected-field accumulator bound, and output-drain window are separate controls. One must not be silently treated as the maximum for another merely because an earlier prototype used the same numeric value.

Any tuning must preserve the Stage 2 memory, backpressure, byte, and window-invariance contracts.

W002-MAT-003.6

Stage 2 uses direct structural parsing rather than a required structural sidecar

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The WASM-002 baseline performs its Stage 2 work directly from the certified source stream. It must not require a precomputed comma/quote/newline position map, binary structural index, hidden cache, or OPFS sidecar before materialization can proceed.

The previously discussed structural-sidecar comparison remains a separate future experiment and must not be introduced into WASM-002 as an unmeasured dependency.

W002-MAT-003.7

The Stage 2 algorithm is browser-first shared Rust core behavior

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The structural parser, row-count semantics, selector dispatch, canonical field serialization, and bounded output-state machine defined by Stage 2 belong in the shared Rust semantic core proven through the browser/WASM path first. A later native CLI host must call the same governed core rather than reimplementing competing materialization semantics.

W002-CONV-001

Conversion is a separate governed operation

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Windows-1252-to-UTF-8 conversion is a distinct governed Work Order operation, separate from UTF-8 certification and separate from analytical materialization. The analyst must explicitly authorize it.

The canonical WASM-002 form is:

SUITCASE: .
WORK ORDER AS "Convert legacy source to UTF-8"
SOURCE "legacy_source.csv"
CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8

CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8 is the terminal operation clause. Exactly one SOURCE is permitted. The same WKO must not contain KEEP, MATERIALIZE, Store/RID/COL alias mutation, MAP, Inventory, repair, cataloging, Work Order composition, or another operation terminal clause.

F-10 conversion entry precondition

Before CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8 may begin character transcoding, Data Sculptor must validate the complete bound source as strict UTF-8 under the same deterministic whole-source certification rules used elsewhere in WASM-002.

  • If the complete source is already valid strict UTF-8, the conversion refuses as unnecessary and publishes no CVT.
  • Only after complete strict UTF-8 validation reaches governed FAIL may Data Sculptor assess the same complete bound source against the frozen Windows-1252 compatibility mapping.
  • Only a source that fails strict UTF-8 and passes the complete Windows-1252 compatibility assessment may proceed to conversion.

A failed analytical Work Order, UTF-8 certification, or materialization never silently invokes this operation. The analyst must explicitly authorize the separate conversion WKO.

W002-CONV-001.1

A failed analytical Work Order must not automatically invoke conversion.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-CONV-001.2

The user must explicitly choose or submit the separate conversion task.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-CONV-001.3

The original source file must remain unchanged.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-CONV-001.4

Successful conversion must create a new UTF-8 artifact with its own governed identity and receipt/evidence.

UNDER REVIEW

W002-CONV-002

Windows-1252 compatibility assessment

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

After strict whole-source UTF-8 certification returns FAIL, the current analytical operation remains refused and Stage 2 must not start. As refusal handling, Data Sculptor performs one separate read-only Windows-1252 compatibility assessment from physical byte offset 0 of the same run-local bound source instance.

The compatibility assessment scans the complete source sequentially under W002-CONV-002.1 through W002-CONV-002.5. It does not transcode, publish a CVT, modify the analyst-owned source, resume materialization, or claim that Windows-1252 is the historical encoding. Its sole governed result is whether the entire byte stream is mappable by the frozen WASM-002 Windows-1252 converter.

If strict UTF-8 certification returned PASS, or did not reach a governed FAIL conclusion, this compatibility assessment is not run.

F-10 conversion classification gate

The conversion operation itself repeats/executes the complete classification gate on its bound source before transcoding:

  1. validate the complete source as strict UTF-8;
  2. if strict UTF-8 passes, refuse conversion as unnecessary;
  3. only after strict UTF-8 fails, scan the complete source against the frozen Windows-1252 mapping;
  4. if any source byte is undefined or unsupported by that mapping, refuse rather than guess; and
  5. begin transcoding only when strict UTF-8 has failed and the complete Windows-1252 compatibility assessment has succeeded.

An undefined/unsupported Windows-1252 byte is therefore a pre-transcoding compatibility-assessment refusal. No CVT candidate may be represented as successfully converted from a source whose compatibility scan found an undefined byte.

The compatibility assessment must not substitute U+FFFD, reinterpret an undefined Windows-1252 byte as ISO-8859-1, or use permissive host/library decoder behavior to make an incompatible source convertible.

W002-CONV-002.1

Compatibility means that the supported deterministic converter can map the observed source bytes under the frozen Windows-1252 rules.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Compatibility means that every physical source byte can be mapped deterministically by the complete normative WASM-002 Windows-1252 mapping in W002-CONV-002.4. Successful EOF produces the governed outcome COMPATIBLE.

No statistical detector, locale rule, browser guess, replacement character, ISO-8859-1 substitution, best-effort decoder, or PRODUCT-scoped glossary text participates as normative authority in this determination.

W002-CONV-002.2

Compatibility must not be described as proof that Windows-1252 was historically or authoritatively the file's original encoding.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

COMPATIBLE means only that the complete byte stream is convertible under Data Sculptor's frozen Windows-1252 mapping. It must not be described as proof that Windows-1252 was historically, authoritatively, or intentionally the source file's original encoding.

W002-CONV-002.3

Bytes undefined by the frozen Windows-1252 mapping must cause the compatibility assessment or conversion task to refuse rather than guess.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

If the compatibility pass encounters a byte that W002-CONV-002.4 defines as undefined, the assessment stops at the first such byte and returns INCOMPATIBLE. Data Sculptor must not substitute a replacement character, reinterpret the byte under another code page, or continue as though conversion were safe.

A later explicit conversion Work Order must apply the same complete WASM-002 mapping and the same refusal rule.

W002-CONV-002.4

Complete normative WASM-002 Windows-1252 byte mapping

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

This requirement is the complete normative Windows-1252 mapping authority for WASM-002. It covers all 256 possible byte values. No PRODUCT-scoped glossary entry or host/library decoder is required to interpret compatibility or conversion.

0x00–0x7F

Every byte 0x00 through 0x7F maps one-to-one to Unicode U+0000 through U+007F.

0x80–0x9F

0x80EURO SIGNU+20AC
0x81UNDEFINED—
0x82SINGLE LOW-9 QUOTATION MARKU+201A
0x83LATIN SMALL LETTER F WITH HOOKU+0192
0x84DOUBLE LOW-9 QUOTATION MARKU+201E
0x85HORIZONTAL ELLIPSISU+2026
0x86DAGGERU+2020
0x87DOUBLE DAGGERU+2021
0x88MODIFIER LETTER CIRCUMFLEX ACCENTU+02C6
0x89PER MILLE SIGNU+2030
0x8ALATIN CAPITAL LETTER S WITH CARONU+0160
0x8BSINGLE LEFT-POINTING ANGLE QUOTATION MARKU+2039
0x8CLATIN CAPITAL LIGATURE OEU+0152
0x8DUNDEFINED—
0x8ELATIN CAPITAL LETTER Z WITH CARONU+017D
0x8FUNDEFINED—
0x90UNDEFINED—
0x91LEFT SINGLE QUOTATION MARKU+2018
0x92RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARKU+2019

0x94RIGHT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARKU+201D

0xA0–0xFF

Every byte 0xA0 through 0xFF maps one-to-one to Unicode U+00A0 through U+00FF.

Undefined-byte rule

The only undefined byte values in this frozen WASM-002 mapping are exactly 0x81, 0x8D, 0x8F, 0x90, and 0x9D. Encountering any one of them makes the complete compatibility assessment INCOMPATIBLE at the first such byte and causes an explicitly run conversion Work Order to refuse before transcoding rather than guess.

These three ranges plus the 32-position table above exhaust the byte domain 0x00–0xFF. No unlisted byte value exists.

W002-CONV-002.5

The compatibility check must itself be bounded and deterministic.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The compatibility check is one bounded-memory deterministic sequential pass from physical source byte offset 0 to EOF unless the first undefined Windows-1252 byte is encountered earlier. Buffer/window size must not change the compatibility outcome or the first undefined-byte offset.

On INCOMPATIBLE, WINDOWS_1252_FIRST_UNDEFINED_BYTE_OFFSET is the zero-based absolute physical source-byte offset of the first undefined byte. On COMPATIBLE, that offset is NOT_APPLICABLE. If the assessment begins but an independent read/host failure prevents a governed compatibility conclusion, the outcome is NOT_AVAILABLE and the first-undefined-byte offset is NOT_AVAILABLE. The assessment itself publishes no converted output.

W002-CONV-003

Help suggestion after failed UTF-8 certification

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Help may suggest the separate CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8 Work Order only when the governed engine emits DS-CNV-001 after a complete compatibility assessment returned COMPATIBLE. The suggestion is therefore derived from a governed diagnostic fact, not from the UTF-8 failure itself.

If the assessment returns INCOMPATIBLE, is NOT_AVAILABLE, or did not run, DS-CNV-001 is not emitted and Help must not invent the conversion recommendation.

P3-08 Help disclosure: when conversion succeeds, Help must state that the published CVT is a new governed source artifact with its own source identity and that converting a refreshed legacy source later will publish another distinct CVT rather than refresh an earlier CVT-backed Store lineage. When a CVT is selected for first materialization, Help must disclose the same consequence before or with the normal materialization guidance: the Store lineage is anchored to the exact CVT filename, not to the analyst-owned pre-conversion filename. Help must not imply hidden lineage continuity across separate CVT artifacts.

W002-CONV-003.1

The suggestion must state that the current analytical task has stopped.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The suggestion must state that the current analytical task has already stopped/refused because strict UTF-8 certification failed. DS-CNV-001 is informational and must not be rendered as though materialization can continue from the failed run.

W002-CONV-003.2

The suggestion must state that the original source has not been changed.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The suggestion must state that the compatibility assessment was read-only and that Data Sculptor did not change the analyst-owned source. Any later successful conversion publishes a separate governed CVT artifact rather than editing the original source in place.

W002-CONV-003.3

The suggestion must describe the source as compatible with the supported Windows-1252 converter, not definitively identified as Windows-1252.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The suggestion must describe the complete source as compatible with Data Sculptor's supported Windows-1252 converter. It must not say that the source was definitively identified as Windows-1252 or imply provenance that the compatibility pass cannot prove.

W002-CONV-003.4

The suggestion must make clear that conversion is a separate user-authorized task.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The suggestion must make clear that conversion is a separate user-authorized Work Order. next_action: RUN_WINDOWS_1252_CONVERSION means that the separate operation is a governed safe option; it is not permission for Data Sculptor to silently transcode, modify the source, or reinterpret the refused analytical Work Order.

W002-CONV-003.5

If the bytes are not compatible with the supported converter, Help must not recommend Windows-1252 conversion as though it were safe.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

If the compatibility outcome is INCOMPATIBLE, NOT_AVAILABLE, or NOT_RUN, Help must not recommend Windows-1252 conversion as though it were safe. In particular, the mere presence of DS-ENC-001 never authorizes that recommendation.

W002-CONV-004

Canonical conversion output

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A successful Windows-1252 conversion task must produce canonical UTF-8 output suitable for later submission to the normal UTF-8 certification and materialization path.

P3-08 lineage consequence: the successful conversion output is a new immutable governed CVT artifact with its own exact physical filename. That CVT filename is the source identity used by later Store routing. A later conversion, including one made from a refreshed analyst-owned legacy source with the same original filename, publishes a different CVT and therefore does not refresh, replace, or continue an earlier CVT-backed Store lineage merely by name association. On first materialization, each distinct CVT begins a new Store lineage unless that exact CVT filename already routes to an existing lineage under the normal Store rules.

F-14 CVT identity and publication: the final converted-source filename is exactly __DS__CVT__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.csv. Conversion writes first to the corresponding W002-STOR-023.1 SCR identity with the same UTC, UUID and .csv extension. Only after bounded conversion completes, the candidate closes/reopens successfully, and the converted bytes satisfy the governed strict UTF-8 requirement may the class token be renamed to CVT. CSV structural interpretation remains governed by the later normal certification/materialization path; CVT publication does not assert that the converted source is structurally valid CSV.

F-10 conversion semantics — encoding conversion only

The conversion operation performs deterministic character transcoding only. It does not parse, repair, normalize, or reinterpret CSV structure.

  • Commas remain commas.
  • Double quotes remain double quotes.
  • Ordinary ASCII bytes retain the same byte value.
  • LF remains LF.
  • CR remains CR.
  • CRLF remains CRLF.
  • Embedded CR/LF bytes are preserved in place; the converter does not decide whether they are record terminators or field content.

Canonical UTF-8 output therefore means deterministic UTF-8 encoding of the accepted source characters, not normalization of line endings, quoting, delimiters, records, headers, or fields.

F-10 BOM rule

  • The published CVT is UTF-8 without a BOM; Data Sculptor does not prepend EF BB BF.
  • If the source failed strict UTF-8 classification, a leading source byte sequence EF BB BF is not blindly stripped as though it were a UTF-8 BOM. Under the Windows-1252 conversion path those source bytes are source data and are mapped according to the frozen Windows-1252 mapping.
  • BOM interpretation remains subordinate to encoding classification rather than acting as a blind prefix-removal rule.
W002-CONV-004.1

The converted artifact must itself be certifiable as UTF-8.

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—
W002-CONV-004.2

The canonical RCP for a successful governed Windows-1252-compatible conversion must identify exactly SOURCE_ENCODING: WINDOWS-1252-COMPATIBLE.

That operation-specific fact is carried within the canonical TXT Receipt governed by W002-RCP-001 through W002-RCP-010. Only that exact serialized spelling is permitted for this key/value pair.

This uses the canonical KEY: VALUE serialization frozen by W002-RCP-005. MATERIALIZED_ENCODING=UTF-8 is not valid canonical Receipt serialization.
