At least one complete HTML Help report using the canonical built-in Data Sculptor presentation must be generated and saved locally from that real event.

W002-HP-ACC-004

Offline durability

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The saved HTML report must remain readable with its canonical built-in Red5Sorcery/Data Sculptor presentation when opened without network access and without access to Data Sculptor or any external presentation resource.

W002-HP-ACC-008

Support-handoff report acceptance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

From a real governed refusal, Data Sculptor must generate one styled HTML Help Report that opens in an ordinary browser without Data Sculptor or network access and contains both a selected-voice explanation and the canonical structured facts needed by a technical reviewer.

W002-HP-ACC-009

Canonical boundary-fact acceptance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

An early-refusal fixture that stops before analytical materialization must demonstrate the exact four Boolean fact names from W002-HELP-004.11 and, when those are the true governed facts, values equivalent to:

source_modified_by_data_sculptor = false
materialization_started = false
analytical_outputs_published = false
store_state_committed = false

Acceptance must also exercise at least one boundary-fact case in which an established Boolean value is unavailable or otherwise carries an applicable governed absence state. The emitted value must use the exact shared JSON string token required by W002-HELP-004.11 (for example "NOT_AVAILABLE") and must not be coerced to false or JSON null. Where a boundary fact is optional and its key is omitted, acceptance must prove that omission is not interpreted as false or as any governed absence token.

The same fixture family must prove that temporary SCR candidates or abandoned/uncommitted debris do not make analytical_outputs_published true.

W002-HP-ACC-010

HLP provenance, multiplicity, and no-automatic-hash acceptance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Acceptance evidence must generate a final HLP using the built-in Red5Sorcery/Data Sculptor presentation and verify its governed __DS__HLP__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.html identity, its visible Provenance section, and exactly one embedded application/json payload with element ID ds-hlp-provenance.

The embedded payload must contain exactly the schema-version-2 fields governed by W002-HELP-009 and must verify the same HLP filename/generation UTC, non-empty ordered diagnostic_ids array, WKO/RCP lineage semantics, selected Help voice, built-in presentation identifier red5sorcery-data-sculptor, built-in presentation version "1", and the exact running Data Sculptor build identifier.

Acceptance must cover: (1) an explicit request for a single diagnostic; (2) one governed Run with multiple included diagnostic events, proving exactly one HLP for the request and event-order parity with diagnostic_ids; and (3) a non-run diagnostic such as Suitcase-validation or WKO-save refusal, proving that non-applicable WKO/RCP lineage is represented by JSON null and visible NOT APPLICABLE rather than invented Run lineage.

Acceptance must also cover all three lineage representations permitted by W002-HELP-009: an exact physical filename when the relationship exists and is known; JSON null when the relationship does not apply; and the exact JSON string "NOT_AVAILABLE" when the relationship applies but its exact filename cannot be obtained. The fixture must prove that null and "NOT_AVAILABLE" are not interchangeable.

Acceptance must prove that the visible Provenance section and machine-readable payload agree semantically; missing, duplicate, malformed, mismatched, non-HTML-safe, disclosure-violating, empty diagnostic_ids, or scope-label-only build provenance must not be accepted. The same acceptance must prove that ordinary HLP generation does not compute or embed an HLP SHA-256 and does not create, refresh, or verify an LCK. Exact-byte HLP integrity remains outside WASM-002 in the later explicit FINGERPRINT/LCK workflow.

W002-HP-ACC-011

Fixed support-handoff disclosure acceptance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Acceptance must prove the fixed support-handoff disclosure boundary with both permitted-context and adversarial headerless fixtures.

A permitted-context fixture must generate an HLP whose diagnostic requires a source filename, one genuinely established relevant source header and/or 1-based column number, bounded execution evidence, and a small executable Work Order excerpt. A governed alias may appear only when the alias itself is necessary to explain the diagnostic, such as an alias collision, ambiguity, or mutation; an unrelated alias must remain excluded. The report must include only the necessary permitted facts while excluding source rows/values, absolute local paths, unrelated headers/aliases/columns, the complete Work Order, Work Order comments, unrelated Suitcase contents, and raw ungoverned stack traces.

A separate headerless-source fixture must place unmistakable sentinel text in the first data row and prove that none of that text appears in the HLP as a header or other disclosed source value. That HLP must show Source header text included: NO and Source values included: NO while still presenting sufficient structural evidence to explain the diagnostic. A genuine-header fixture must prove that a necessary established header may appear with Source header text included: YES. Alias fixtures must similarly prove truthful Governed alias text included: YES only when necessary and NO otherwise.

Every fixture must verify the remaining frozen Disclosure declarations from W002-HELP-010. WASM-002 must expose no control that changes this fixed disclosure policy.

W002-HP-ACC-012

Cross-session source-continuity Help acceptance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

An acceptance fixture must present Help with a suspected cross-session source-change scenario and verify that the explanation asks whether the source may have been edited/replaced/sorted/re-exported/synchronized, distinguishes no evidence from INVENTORY metadata evidence and stronger explicit fingerprint evidence, and never claims that unchanged filename or unchanged INVENTORY metadata proves byte identity.

A no-evidence fixture must state that continuity cannot be independently verified. An INVENTORY fixture with changed source byte length or last-modified metadata must describe the difference as evidence that the source may have changed, not as a cryptographic conclusion. The fixture must also confirm that ordinary WASM-002 materialization did not automatically hash the source as part of this edge-case protection.

W002-HP-ACC-013

Diagnostic-registry and Help cross-validation acceptance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

WASM-002 acceptance must retain the validated diagnostics.json used by the accepted build and verify its exact version-1 schema, canonical sort order, unique permanent IDs, fixed-token grammars, and disjoint required/optional fact declarations.

At least one real governed diagnostic fixture must prove that the emitted semantic core matches the matching registry entry and that all required facts are present while no undeclared fact key is emitted. Negative build-validation fixtures must prove deterministic failure for malformed/duplicate registry entries, an engine diagnostic definition absent from the registry, fixed semantic disagreement, an undeclared emitted fact, a Help-catalog diagnostic ID absent from the registry, and a Help placeholder not declared for its matching diagnostic.

F-17 runtime completeness fixtures: missing required facts are no longer treated as a malformed event that may leak to Help. Fault injection must prove deterministic substitution with DS-HLP-001, including exact intended_diagnostic_id and sorted missing_required_facts, with no partially populated intended diagnostic emitted. Separately, a valid registered diagnostic omitted from help_messages.json must remain a valid build/runtime condition and must exercise the Generic Technical fallback rather than build failure or diagnostic suppression.

F-22 QA-independence acceptance boundary: acceptance must prove the registry/engine/Help wiring and generic invariants without circularly presenting the implementation-delivered registry as an independent oracle for its own condition-to-Diagnostic-ID allocations. Representative governed fixtures must trace condition → emitted Diagnostic ID → matching registry semantic core → required/optional fact discipline → Help lookup/rendering. Every condition-to-ID or required-fact mapping explicitly frozen elsewhere in this PRD remains independently testable and must match that PRD contract.

For allocations not independently pinned by this PRD, WASM-002 does not require a duplicate QA-owned registry that restates every condition-to-ID choice. Passing this acceptance gate therefore demonstrates registry integrity, engine↔registry semantic agreement, fact completeness/legality, Help-catalog wiring, F-17 fail-safe behavior, and representative end-to-end diagnostic routing; it must not be reported as exhaustive independent proof that every possible runtime condition was assigned the semantically correct Diagnostic ID. That residual independence limitation is an accepted WASM-002 risk.

F-23 embedded Help-catalog release fixture: acceptance must build the released HTML from a validated help_messages.json, verify exactly one non-executable application/json payload with element ID ds-help-catalog, and include adversarial catalog text containing literal < / script-like delimiter content to prove HTML-safe embedding. Runtime instrumentation must prove that Help lookup reads only the embedded payload and performs no network, filesystem, Suitcase, or adjacent-file fetch for the Help catalog. A missing, malformed, mismatched, or unsafe embedded catalog must fail build acceptance.

W002-WKO-007

Work Order syntax is the analytical contract

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

If a value, reference, option, or instruction changes what Data Sculptor analytically does, that intent must be represented in governed Work Order text or in a separately governed artifact explicitly referenced by that Work Order. Browser permission, directory selection, UI focus, a highlighted file, an alias display, or another GUI gesture must not silently become analytical intent.

For WASM-002, every executable saved WKO begins with the common preamble:

SUITCASE: .
WORK ORDER AS "<non-whitespace alias>"

Ignoring blank lines and governed comments, the WKO must then parse completely under exactly one of these seven executable operation grammars:

OperationGoverned DS-STEPS structure after the common preamble
MATERIALIZESOURCE "..."; optional MAP "..."; KEEP; one or more selectors; terminal MATERIALIZE.
INVENTORYterminal INVENTORY only.
UPDATE ALIASESexactly one Store-state selector: SOURCE "..." or MAP "..."; one or more governed alias mutations; terminal UPDATE ALIASES.
REPAIR MAPexactly one MAP "<exact current Store MAP filename>"; terminal REPAIR MAP.
REPAIR WORK ORDER REGISTRYterminal REPAIR WORK ORDER REGISTRY only.
CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8exactly one SOURCE "..."; terminal CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8.
CATALOG STORESterminal CATALOG STORES only.

Each operation-specific numbered requirement remains authoritative for its detailed selectors, preconditions, mutations, publication semantics, and acceptance behavior. This requirement freezes the cross-operation boundary: unknown semantic lines refuse; clauses from another operation grammar refuse unless the selected operation explicitly defines them; there is no best-effort interpretation and no silent cross-operation mixing.

Lexical token separation. DS-STEPS keywords are matched ASCII case-insensitively; canonical examples render them uppercase. Wherever two adjacent lexical tokens would otherwise run together, they must be separated by one or more ASCII SPACE (0x20) or horizontal TAB (0x09) characters. Leading SPACE/TAB indentation is semantically neutral. Thus REPAIR MAP, SOURCE "crime.csv", and COLUMN 7 are valid tokenizations, while REPAIRMAP, SOURCE"crime.csv", and UPDATE_ALIASES are not alternate DS-STEPS spellings. Quoted-string contents are never case-folded or whitespace-normalized merely because keywords are case-insensitive.

The browser may authorize resources, edit text, validate, save, invoke Run, display evidence, and provide Help. Authorization to access a resource is not authorization to use that resource analytically.

W002-WKO-008

Every executable Work Order explicitly declares its Suitcase

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

For WASM-002, every executable saved Work Order must contain the exact portable declaration SUITCASE: .. The dot means the filesystem directory that physically contains the saved WKO artifact being executed. A Work Order lacking this declaration must not be treated as an executable WASM-002 Work Order.

The declaration is analytical/execution syntax, not a substitute for browser filesystem permission. The host must still possess valid access to the directory before execution can proceed.

Help obligation: Data Sculptor Help must explain SUITCASE: . in plain language: the saved Work Order uses the folder that contains that WKO as its Suitcase; the dot means “this folder”; ordinary Work Order file references are therefore portable and Suitcase-relative; and browser/host permission to the folder is granted separately. Help must not teach an absolute machine path as the normal replacement for ..

W002-WKO-009

Ordinary Work Order file references are Suitcase-relative

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Unless another numbered requirement explicitly governs a different reference mechanism, file references in an executable WASM-002 Work Order resolve relative to the declared Suitcase. A portable Work Order must not depend on an absolute machine-specific path to identify ordinary Suitcase files.

Resolution must be deterministic in browser and later native hosts. Moving an intact Suitcase to another permitted filesystem location must not change the logical meaning of the Work Order solely because the parent machine path changed.

W002-WKO-009.1

WASM-002 SOURCE eligibility is exact and root-bounded

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A WASM-002 SOURCE clause names exactly one physical regular file in the Suitcase root by exact filename only. It must not name an absolute path, drive or UNC path, subdirectory, path containing / or \, traversal such as .., URL/URI, or another external reference. Resolution uses the exact Unicode-scalar filename identity and reference-bounded rules frozen by F-15; no case-folding, normalization, trimming, or filesystem-equivalence search is permitted.

The only eligible WASM-002 SOURCE kinds are:

  1. Analyst-owned CSV: a regular Suitcase-root file whose exact filename does not begin with the reserved exact prefix __DS__ and whose final extension is .csv under ASCII case-insensitive extension recognition. Thus .csv, .CSV, and mixed-case equivalents are candidate CSV extensions. This case-insensitivity applies only to extension recognition; the complete filename reference remains exact. If the physical file is crime.CSV, a differently cased full filename does not become an alternate reference to it.
  2. Governed converted source: a successfully published CVT whose exact canonical identity and class-specific publication/validity predicate satisfy W002-CONV-004, W002-STOR-023, and PB-STOR-008. A filename that merely resembles a CVT is not sufficient.

No other governed semantic class is eligible as SOURCE in WASM-002, even when its physical serialization is CSV. In particular, COL, RID, MAP, CAT, INV, RCP, HLP, CER, SCR, RCV, and WKO artifacts cannot be reintroduced as SOURCE merely because their bytes or extension appear compatible.

A recognized .csv extension establishes only candidate SOURCE form. It does not certify encoding or CSV structure; the normal strict UTF-8 and structural certification contracts still govern after source resolution. Conversely, CSV-like bytes stored under a non-CSV analyst-owned extension are not an eligible WASM-002 SOURCE.

W002-WKO-010

WIP and WKO are distinct Work Order lifecycle states

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

WIP is the editable, non-executable Work Order state. WKO is the saved, validated, immutable Work Order artifact that may become a Run target. Validation establishes that a Work Order is structurally eligible to run; it does not guarantee that runtime conditions will succeed.

Loading a WKO for inspection does not make it mutable. If its instruction text is changed, the editor must treat the edited text as a new WIP derived from the original WKO. The original WKO bytes and physical identity remain unchanged, and the derived WIP cannot Run until saved as a new WKO.

F-08 Run distinction: the browser Run action invokes one selected saved immutable WKO that is eligible under the governed WKO-registry rules. No ordinary WASM-002 WKO contains a textual RUN line merely to execute itself. The DS-STEPS token RUN is reserved for future saved-Work-Order composition under W002-WKO-011 and is not repurposed as the browser execution trigger.

W002-WKO-013

WASM-002 executes one saved Work Order without Work Order chaining

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

For WASM-002, one saved immutable WKO is one top-level executable request. It must not invoke, include, chain, or execute another WKO. The governed RUN composition operation and equivalent nested-orchestration constructs are not executable in WASM-002.

If a saved WKO contains composition syntax, validation must refuse before analytical execution begins. The canonical diagnostic and Help path must explain that Work Order composition is deferred rather than treating the syntax as arbitrary text, silently ignoring it, or partially executing surrounding instructions.

This scope cut does not prohibit one Work Order from selecting and materializing multiple columns in the single Stage 2 operation defined by WASM-002.

W002-WKO-012

Materialization COL alias assignment uses AS; standalone alias maintenance uses UPDATE ALIASES

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Within the WASM-002 DS-STEPS materialization form, an analyst assigns or changes the alias of a selected materialized COL with the optional same-line clause AS "alias" under W002-STEPS-005. This syntax is part of the governed Work Order and is not a GUI gesture. A single KEEP block may therefore assign aliases to multiple selected columns in one governed materialization.

Automatic source-header COL aliases and inherited rematerialization aliases are resolved first; explicit AS clauses then determine requested successor COL aliases before complete Store-MAP validation and publication.

Revision BD freezes alias-only creation/replacement with UPDATE ALIASES and explicit historical Store-MAP selection with MAP "<exact Store MAP filename>". Revision BE completes the bounded alias lifecycle with explicit CLEAR ... ALIAS and RESET ... ALIAS forms under W002-WKO-012.5 through W002-WKO-012.6. Empty-string AS "" is not the clearing syntax.

W002-WKO-012.1

Canonical standalone alias-maintenance Work Order uses UPDATE ALIASES

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The canonical alias-only Store metadata forms are:

SUITCASE: .
WORK ORDER AS "Rename crime store"
SOURCE "35100178.csv"
STORE AS "Crime Statistics"
UPDATE ALIASES

or, when the analyst intentionally selects one exact Store snapshot:

SUITCASE: .
WORK ORDER AS "Rename crime store"
MAP "__DS__MAP__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.csv"
STORE AS "Crime Statistics"
UPDATE ALIASES

UPDATE ALIASES is the explicit terminal commitment clause for an alias-only Work Order. The WKO must identify exactly one Store-state base using either SOURCE "..." for ordinary Store-aware current-state selection or MAP "..." for exact Store-MAP selection, never both. At least one supported alias mutation clause must occur after the Store-state selector and before UPDATE ALIASES.

An alias-only Work Order must not contain KEEP, MATERIALIZE, INVENTORY, conversion, Store repair, Work Order registry repair, cataloging, deferred Work Order composition, or another operation's terminal clause. Alias maintenance changes governed human-facing metadata only.

W002-WKO-012.2

STORE AS, RID AS, and COL ... AS are the canonical alias-replacement clauses

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Within an alias-only UPDATE ALIASES Work Order, the canonical mutation clauses are:

STORE AS "Crime Statistics"
RID AS "Row Number"
COL "Crime Rate" AS "Police-Reported Crime Rate"

STORE AS "..." replaces the selected Store snapshot's store_alias. RID AS "..." replaces its rid_alias. COL "<reference>" AS "..." replaces the alias of exactly one existing mapped COL.

The COL reference resolves under W002-STOR-021: it may be the exact physical column_filename or one unique current COL alias from the selected Store MAP. Missing, ambiguous, non-COL, or conflicting resolution must refuse rather than guess. One Work Order may update the Store alias, RID alias, and multiple distinct COL aliases together, provided the complete successor state satisfies all existing alias uniqueness/shadowing rules.

W002-WKO-012.3

MAP "<filename>" is the exact historical Store-MAP selector

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The canonical explicit Store-MAP selection clause is:

MAP "__DS__MAP__20260920T184512347Z__<uuid-v4>.csv"

The value is always the exact physical filename of one structurally valid immutable Store MAP. It is not a Store alias, WKO alias, timestamp shorthand, UUID-only selector, or latest expression. For MATERIALIZE, if present, the clause occurs immediately after SOURCE and before KEEP. It overrides automatic Store-MAP inheritance and binds the run to exactly the named Store snapshot.

For alias-only maintenance, the Work Order uses either SOURCE "..." or MAP "..." as its Store-state selector, not both. For materialization, SOURCE "..." remains mandatory and an optional MAP "..." supplies the exact historical/current Store-state base. Validation must refuse an incompatible source/MAP pairing or a MAP that is not a valid Store-MAP profile.

Health rule: explicit historical selection does not override the current Store-lineage health gate. The selected lineage must currently be VALID and every RID/COL binding referenced by the named MAP must currently be present and valid. Otherwise the operation refuses. This applies equally to MATERIALIZE and UPDATE ALIASES.

F-05/P2-01 source-compatibility predicate: for materialization, an explicitly named MAP is compatible only when the mandatory Work Order SOURCE exactly equals the one common source_filename carried by that Store MAP. If the exact filenames differ, validation refuses before the F-04 existing-Store cardinality gate in W002-MAT-002.6. Equal row count never authorizes a different source to enter the selected Store lineage.

W002-WKO-012.4

Alias-only execution publishes one complete successor Store MAP and no rewritten data artifacts

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

A successful UPDATE ALIASES operation begins from the selected complete Store MAP, applies only the requested alias replacements in memory, validates the complete resulting Store state, writes the successor MAP under governed SCR, closes and reopens it, validates it fully, and promotes it to a new immutable MAP last. That successful promotion is the alias-update commit point.

The operation must preserve the selected Store's physical RID and COL filenames and bytes, source-column keys, row order, cardinality, and lineage except for the human-facing alias fields explicitly changed by the Work Order. It must not reread source data rows merely to change aliases, must not create RID/COL artifacts, and must not rewrite or delete the inherited MAP. The prior MAP remains visible historical state.

If validation or MAP publication fails, no successor alias state becomes current. The failure is reported through the governed diagnostic/Help path and any incomplete candidate remains subject to the retained-SCR failure-evidence rules in W002-STOR-023.1; WASM-002 does not emit RCV.

Revision BM E-02 integration: when the alias-only operation uses an explicitly named historical Store MAP, publication is permitted only if the Store lineage currently evaluates VALID and every RID/COL binding referenced by that named MAP is currently present and valid. An older MAP cannot be used to bypass current damage.

P3-06 validation depth: because UPDATE ALIASES does not consume RID/COL analytical contents, its Store-health and binding checks use Tier 1 under W002-STOR-019.10. The operation must not scan every RID/COL record merely to change aliases. This does not weaken later operations that actually consume those artifacts; they must perform the applicable Tier 2 validation before relying on the contents.

W002-WKO-ACC-007

Standalone Store/RID/COL alias maintenance acceptance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Acceptance must establish a Store with one RID and at least three materialized COLs, then execute an alias-only Work Order that changes the Store alias, RID alias, and at least two COL aliases in one UPDATE ALIASES operation. One COL must be targeted by its unique current alias and another by its exact physical COL filename.

The fixture must prove that exactly one complete successor Store MAP becomes current; prior MAP, RID, and COL artifacts remain byte-for-byte unchanged; no source-data row read is required; no new RID/COL artifact is published; and the successor MAP contains exactly the requested aliases while preserving all physical bindings and logical source-column keys. Missing/ambiguous COL references and successor alias collisions must refuse without publishing a successor MAP.

F-23 CLEAR/RESET alias fixtures: acceptance must separately exercise CLEAR STORE ALIAS, CLEAR RID ALIAS, CLEAR COL "<reference>" ALIAS, RESET STORE ALIAS, RESET RID ALIAS, and RESET COL "<reference>" ALIAS. Each CLEAR fixture must prove that the successor MAP stores the governed empty alias without renaming or rewriting the referenced artifact. Each RESET fixture must prove restoration of the exact deterministic default governed by W002-WKO-012.6 and W002-STOR-019.7, including the oversized-header operational fallback where applicable.

The fixtures must prove that CLEAR and RESET require no source-data row read, publish exactly one complete successor Store MAP on success, leave the predecessor MAP/RID/COL bytes unchanged, and deterministically refuse duplicate mutation of the same alias field or a reset/default value that fails the complete successor alias validity/uniqueness/shadowing rules.

W002-WKO-ACC-008

Explicit historical Store-MAP selection acceptance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Acceptance must create at least two valid Store MAP snapshots for one Store, then prove that a Work Order containing MAP "<older exact Store MAP filename>" binds to that exact older snapshot even though a newer valid MAP exists.

An alias-only fixture must publish its successor from the explicitly named older base rather than from the newer automatic current state. A materialization fixture must retain mandatory SOURCE "..." while using the explicit MAP as its Store-state base. The tests must also prove refusal for a missing MAP, malformed MAP, WKO-MAP profile supplied as Store MAP, and source/MAP incompatibility. No implementation may substitute the newest MAP after an explicit MAP clause has validated.

F-21 chronology acceptance: the fixture must use at least three successive valid MAP snapshots for one Store so that an explicitly selected older base and a distinct pre-run current MAP both exist. Merely selecting/validating the older MAP must leave current authority unchanged. A successful governed operation from that older base must then publish exactly one new successor whose requested state is derived from the named older base, whose publication UTC is later than the pre-run current chronology predecessor, and which becomes current under ordinary greatest-UTC selection. The selected historical MAP and the formerly current MAP must remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

Acceptance must prove that later mappings/aliases present only in the formerly current MAP are not silently merged into the historical-base successor unless the Work Order explicitly recreates them. Receipt evidence must identify the exact operation base and exact published successor through the already-frozen operation-specific Receipt fields. No additional warning/permission gate or informational diagnostic is required merely because the analyst explicitly chose a historical base.

W002-WKO-012.5

CLEAR ... ALIAS deliberately removes a human-facing alias

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Within an alias-only UPDATE ALIASES Work Order, the canonical clearing forms are:

CLEAR STORE ALIAS
CLEAR RID ALIAS
CLEAR COL "<reference>" ALIAS

CLEAR deliberately stores the empty string in the corresponding alias field of the successor Store MAP. It does not restore a default alias. An empty-string replacement such as STORE AS "", RID AS "", or COL "..." AS "" is not the canonical clearing form and must be rejected by the bounded WASM-002 grammar.

For CLEAR COL, <reference> resolves against the selected pre-mutation Store MAP by exact physical column_filename or one unique current COL alias under W002-STOR-021. All COL references in one UPDATE ALIASES Work Order are resolved before any mutation is applied so clause order cannot change target identity. Missing, ambiguous, duplicate-target, or non-COL references must refuse. Clearing an alias never renames, rewrites, or deletes the underlying RID/COL artifact and never changes physical identity.

W002-WKO-012.6

RESET ... ALIAS restores the deterministic default alias

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Within an alias-only UPDATE ALIASES Work Order, the canonical reset forms are:

RESET STORE ALIAS
RESET RID ALIAS
RESET COL "<reference>" ALIAS

RESET STORE ALIAS restores the Store MAP's common exact source_filename. RESET RID ALIAS restores the literal RID. RESET COL "<reference>" ALIAS restores that mapped COL's deterministic operational default defined by W002-STOR-019.7 from its exact recorded source_header and physical source ordinal: the exact header when it contains at most 1,024 Unicode scalar values, or the deterministic Column <LETTERS> fallback/disambiguation rule when the recorded header exceeds that boundary. RESET never substitutes the potentially oversized exact header into the alias field merely because that header remains authoritative source evidence.

RESET is therefore distinct from CLEAR. The restored value must pass the same governed alias validity, uniqueness, and shadowing rules as any explicit alias. If the deterministic default is empty or conflicts in the complete successor Store MAP, RESET must refuse except for the narrow oversized-header fallback/disambiguation rule already frozen in W002-STOR-019.7; Data Sculptor must not otherwise invent a suffix, alternate spelling, or substitute.

AS, CLEAR, and RESET mutations may coexist in one Work Order when they target distinct alias fields; duplicate mutation of the same alias field in one Work Order must refuse. A successful operation publishes exactly one complete successor Store MAP under the existing UPDATE ALIASES commit contract.

W002-STEPS-001

Canonical WASM-002 DS-STEPS materialization form

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The canonical WASM-002 materialization Work Order form is:

# Optional human comment
SUITCASE: .
WORK ORDER AS "Prepare monthly crime data"
SOURCE "crime.csv"
[MAP "__DS__MAP__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.csv"]

KEEP
  HEADER "REF_DATE" AS "Year"      # reporting year
  HEADER "GEO"
  COLUMN 7 AS "Crime Rate"

MATERIALIZE

SUITCASE: . is governed by W002-WKO-008.

WORK ORDER AS "..." is mandatory for an executable/saved WASM-002 Work Order and declares the immutable human-facing WKO alias governed by W002-STEPS-001.1.

SOURCE "..." names the exact Suitcase-root source file.

MAP "..." is optional with cardinality 0..1. If present, it occurs immediately after SOURCE and before KEEP, names one exact physical governed Store MAP filename, and binds the run to that exact current or historical Store lineage subject to W002-STOR-019.3 and W002-WKO-012.3. If absent, the Store-aware exact-source routing rules apply.

KEEP is the bare governed keyword and introduces one or more column selectors. KEEP: is not valid WASM-002 syntax. Each selector is either HEADER "..." or COLUMN n and may optionally end with AS "...".

MATERIALIZE is the explicit terminal commitment verb. Duplicate structural clauses refuse. An empty KEEP refuses. After MATERIALIZE, only blank lines or comments may follow; a trailing comment on the physical MATERIALIZE line is permitted because comments are removed from the semantic token stream.

# comments are governed by W002-STEPS-001.2. No RID/row-index clause appears in the Work Order. If this materialization establishes a new Store, the engine automatically generates exactly one RID artifact under W002-RID-002 and W002-RID-008. If it extends an existing Store, the existing RID is reused subject to the Store health/cardinality rules.

This requirement freezes the bounded keyword structure and selector forms shown above for BM integration. Other complete-language lexical features remain outside this bounded syntax freeze unless separately specified.

F-08 common-grammar boundary: MATERIALIZE is one of the seven executable WASM-002 operation grammars governed by W002-WKO-007. Its optional MAP clause remains in the frozen position immediately after SOURCE and before KEEP. The terminal MATERIALIZE clause is DS-STEPS syntax; the browser's Run action is not written into the Work Order.

F-20 bounded KEEP: the canonical KEEP block contains at least one and at most 16,384 selectors, and after resolution those selectors must identify at least one and at most 16,384 distinct source columns. This is the complete WASM-002 selection-width bound.

W002-STEPS-001.1

WORK ORDER AS declares the immutable human-facing Work Order alias

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

An executable or saved WASM-002 Work Order must contain exactly one top-level clause:

WORK ORDER AS "<alias>"

In canonical forms it appears after SUITCASE: . and before the operation-specific source/selector clauses. The decoded alias must be non-empty. The quoted alias may contain spaces and ordinary UTF-8 phrase text subject to the governed string-literal rules. The alias affects display and governed alias resolution only; it does not replace the WKO filename/UUID as physical execution identity.

The alias is stored in the immutable WKO bytes and is published into the current WKO MAP when the WKO save transaction commits. Changing the alias therefore requires saving a new WKO under the frozen WKO lifecycle. No valid executable/saved WKO in WASM-002 is unaliased.

P3-10 alias-content rule: “non-empty” means that, after decoding the quoted string literal, the alias must contain at least one non-whitespace character. An alias consisting only of whitespace refuses Work Order validation. Data Sculptor must not trim, collapse, normalize, or otherwise rewrite leading or trailing whitespace in an otherwise valid alias; the decoded alias text remains authoritative and is preserved exactly in the immutable WKO and governed WKO MAP.

W002-STEPS-001.2

# introduces a DS-STEPS line comment outside double-quoted strings

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Outside a double-quoted string, the first # on a line begins a comment that continues through the line's LF terminator. Whole-line comments and trailing comments are permitted. Comment text has no execution semantics and is ignored by the DS-STEPS parser after lexical recognition.

A # inside a double-quoted string is ordinary string content and does not begin a comment; for example WORK ORDER AS "Analysis #3" and HEADER "CATEGORY #" preserve the hash character. WASM-002 defines no block-comment syntax.

Comments are preserved byte-for-byte in the saved immutable WKO TXT. Editing, adding, or removing a comment changes the WKO bytes and therefore requires saving a new WKO artifact even though analytical semantics may remain unchanged.

W002-STEPS-002

HEADER selects by exact decoded source-header value

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

HEADER "name" resolves against the exact decoded header values established for the certified source. Header equality is exact Unicode scalar-value sequence equality under PB-STOR-010: Data Sculptor performs no case folding, locale folding, Unicode normalization, trimming, or filesystem-style comparison.

A selector that matches no source header must refuse. If the same exact decoded header sequence occurs in more than one source column, the header selector is ambiguous and must refuse rather than choose by position, discovery order, normalization, case-insensitive similarity, or another heuristic.

An analyst can disambiguate duplicate exact header text with the 1-based COLUMN n selector.

F-20 selector identity: HEADER always matches the authoritative exact decoded source header. It never matches an operational fallback name such as Column AA, a generated collision-disambiguation suffix, a COL alias, or a truncated form of the source header.

W002-STEPS-003

COLUMN selects by 1-based source ordinal

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

COLUMN n identifies the source column by 1-based ordinal position. COLUMN 1 is the first source column. Zero, negative values, non-integers, and ordinals greater than the source width must refuse.

Ordinal selection does not suppress source metadata: Data Sculptor must still resolve and record the selected column's actual decoded source header in the successor MAP.

W002-STEPS-004

HEADER and COLUMN selectors may be mixed but may not select one source column twice

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

One KEEP block may contain any supported mixture of HEADER and COLUMN selectors. Selector order expresses the analyst's requested selection order for the governed operation.

After resolution, two or more selectors that identify the same physical source column constitute a duplicate selection and must refuse before materialization. Data Sculptor must not materialize the same source column twice merely because it was named once by header and once by ordinal.

W002-STEPS-005

AS assigns the resulting materialized-column alias

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The optional clause AS "alias" belongs to the immediately preceding HEADER or COLUMN selector and expresses an intentional human-facing alias assignment in the governed Work Order.

For a logical source column not present in the inherited MAP, omission of AS uses the exact source header as the default alias. For a logical source column already present in the inherited MAP, omission of AS preserves the inherited alias. An explicit AS overrides either default for the successor MAP.

W002-STEPS-006

The complete successor MAP must contain unique aliases

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

After inheritance, selector resolution, default-alias application, rematerialization continuity, and all explicit AS clauses are applied, every alias in the complete successor MAP must identify exactly one logical materialized column.

If two different logical columns would have the same alias, including a collision with an inherited mapping, validation must refuse unless the Work Order has explicitly resolved the conflict through supported governed syntax. Data Sculptor must not invent suffixes such as Year_2, use last-write-wins behavior, or silently shadow an existing alias.

F-20 narrow generated-name exception: the prohibition on invented suffixes applies to ordinary source-header defaults and analyst-authored aliases. The only automatic suffixing permitted in WASM-002 is deterministic disambiguation of an oversized-header operational fallback under W002-STOR-019.7. That mechanism is not an alias-repair heuristic and must not be applied to an explicit AS value or to a short exact source-header default.

W002-STEPS-007

MATERIALIZE commits the resolved KEEP set to the governed structural pass

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

MATERIALIZE is the explicit commitment verb for this WASM-002 DS-STEPS form. The KEEP selectors express which source columns belong in the operation; they do not themselves authorize data-row materialization.

Before the bounded structural pass begins, the source, all selectors, actual source ordinals/headers, requested aliases, inherited alias state, and resulting alias uniqueness must be resolved and validated. Successful multi-column execution then follows the one-pass materialization contract.

W002-STEPS-008

The Store MAP records resolved truth rather than selector spelling

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The successor Store MAP must record the fully resolved materialization result using the frozen eight-column schema store_alias,rid_filename,rid_alias,source_filename,source_column_number,source_header,alias,column_filename, regardless of whether the analyst selected a column with HEADER or COLUMN.

For example, COLUMN 7 AS "Crime Rate" records the Store alias, RID filename/alias, common source filename, source ordinal 7, the actual decoded header found at column 7, alias Crime Rate, and the newly generated physical COL filename. DS-STEPS expresses intent; the Store MAP persists the resolved durable mapping truth.

W002-STEPS-009

DS-STEPS materialization syntax acceptance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Acceptance must cover: one column selected by exact header; one column selected by 1-based ordinal; mixed header/ordinal selectors in one KEEP block; multiple columns materialized in one governed structural pass; AS alias assignment; default header aliasing; inherited-alias preservation on rematerialization; explicit alias replacement on rematerialization; duplicate-header ambiguity refusal; invalid ordinal refusal; duplicate resolved-column refusal; and duplicate successor-alias refusal.

Acceptance must also prove that the generated successor MAP records the same resolved source filename, source ordinal, actual source header, resulting alias, and physical COL identity whether a column was selected by header or by ordinal.

For a new Store, both the single-column and multi-column materialization fixtures must contain no RID/row-index instruction yet must automatically publish exactly one RID artifact. For a later permitted same-Store materialization, the fixture must likewise contain no RID instruction and must reuse the original RID without publishing another.

Damaged-lineage Help acceptance: fixtures must prove that exact source routing to an INVALID Store, and to a DEGRADED Store whose every mapped COL is broken, refuses ordinary materialization without silently treating the source as unseen. The canonical diagnostic/Help evidence must identify the blocked lineage/current MAP and preserve the frozen analyst-owned exits: external restoration under the original governed physical filename followed by governed validation; source rename to begin a distinct new Store lineage; or moving all lineage MAPs out of the active Suitcase to retire that lineage from routing. The all-COLs-broken fixture must warn that moving only the latest MAP is insufficient. No fixture may imply a new Data Sculptor recovery command, automatic RID regeneration, silent replacement of the damaged lineage, or historical byte identity based only on a restored filename.

P3-06 validation-tier acceptance: acceptance must prove that a routine routing/status or alias-only path can use Tier 1 without an end-to-end scan of every RID/COL value, while an operation that consumes artifact contents performs Tier 2 before relying on them. Fixtures must include: a RID that passes Tier 1 but fails Tier 2 because its declared N/sequence is internally wrong beyond the Tier-1 boundary; a COL that passes Tier 1 but fails Tier 2 because its data-record count or CSV body is invalid beyond the Tier-1 boundary; and a REPAIR MAP fixture proving that the Tier-2 failure set determines exactly which COL bindings are removed.

P3-07 routing acceptance: fixtures must prove that routing discovers a lineage from a structurally valid Store MAP regardless of whether later Store-health evaluation is VALID, DEGRADED, or INVALID. A separate fixture must present no routable lineage together with at least one structurally malformed Store-MAP-class artifact in the active Suitcase and prove that ordinary materialization refuses before publishing a new RID or first Store MAP, while Help identifies the malformed MAP artifact or artifacts. No fixture may treat an all-MAPs-damaged condition as permission for a silent replacement lineage.

F-08 cross-operation grammar acceptance: fixtures must prove the common preamble, ASCII-case-insensitive keywords, exact quoted-value preservation, required SPACE/TAB token separation, unknown-line refusal, one-operation-per-WKO refusal, and separation between DS-STEPS terminal phrases and Receipt OPERATION tokens. At least one fixture for each of the seven executable operations must prove that its canonical structure validates while an otherwise similar WKO containing another operation's terminal clause refuses. Separate fixtures must prove that browser Run does not require a textual RUN clause and that parsed RUN composition syntax refuses as deferred before analytical execution.

P2-04 restoration-language acceptance: Help, diagnostics, UI text, and acceptance evidence may say that a file restored under the exact governed physical filename passed the required validation tier and may therefore re-enter use. They must not state or imply that filename equality alone proves restoration of the historical original bytes. If stronger historical-byte identity is desired, Help may point to the separately governed explicit fingerprint/LCK direction rather than silently hashing ordinary Store artifacts.

F-20 selector/name/width acceptance: fixtures must additionally prove that HEADER resolves only against exact decoded source-header text and never against an operational fallback/default alias; a KEEP selecting all 16,384 columns is valid; a source wider than 16,384 refuses before data-row materialization; and RESET of an oversized-header COL restores the deterministic operational fallback rather than the exact oversized header as alias text.

F-03 Store-health and REPAIR MAP acceptance set

  • Target required: REPAIR MAP without exactly one current Store MAP target refuses.
  • Historical target: a structurally valid but non-current historical Store MAP refuses for repair.
  • Wrong profile: a WKO MAP supplied as the repair target refuses.
  • DEGRADED repair: one or more broken COL bindings are removed while every valid binding and the exact RID identity are preserved.
  • All COLs broken: repair refuses, publishes no successor MAP, and the Store remains DEGRADED.
  • Malformed newest MAP: current-state resolution falls back to the greatest earlier structurally valid MAP in the same lineage and reports the malformed artifact.
  • Missing COL in current valid MAP: no fallback occurs; the current MAP remains current and the Store evaluates DEGRADED.
  • Missing RID in current valid MAP: no fallback occurs; the current MAP remains current and the Store evaluates INVALID.
  • Original RID externally restored: the Store is re-evaluated after governed validation without Data Sculptor creating or inferring a replacement RID.
  • No silent fork: neither DEGRADED nor INVALID permits ordinary materialization to create a replacement Store for the same routed lineage.
W002-WKO-ACC-003

Suitcase-relative Work Order portability acceptance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

An acceptance fixture must execute a saved WKO containing SUITCASE: . and ordinary Suitcase-relative file references, then move the intact fixture Suitcase to a different permitted parent path and execute the same saved WKO again. Resolution must identify the same logical Suitcase files without editing the WKO to insert the new absolute machine path.

W002-WKO-ACC-004

WIP/WKO lifecycle acceptance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Acceptance evidence must show that an editable WIP cannot Run; saving a valid WIP produces a distinct immutable WKO Run target; loading that WKO and changing instruction text creates a new non-runnable WIP; and the original WKO bytes, filename, identity, and provenance remain unchanged.

F-02 alias-registry lifecycle acceptance: a first save for an unused alias must publish a successor WKO MAP containing exactly one CURRENT row for that alias. Saving a second valid WKO with the same exact alias must surface exactly Replace alias target and Cancel. The Cancel fixture must leave the predecessor WKO MAP authoritative and must not commit the pending WKO/WKO-MAP pair as a registry update. The Replace fixture must publish a successor WKO MAP in which the former owner is DEPRECATED, the new WKO is the sole CURRENT row for that alias, and any earlier deprecated history remains preserved. The former WKO bytes and filename and every predecessor WKO MAP must remain unchanged. Alias resolution against the successor registry must resolve to the new CURRENT row and never to a DEPRECATED row. A malformed fixture containing more than one CURRENT row for one exact alias must fail structural validation rather than choose by filename UTC, modified time, discovery order, or row order.

P2-03 WKO-registry clock acceptance: using a deterministic injected clock seam, acceptance must prove that a successor WKO MAP publishes only when the observed transaction UTC is strictly greater than the current structurally valid WKO MAP UTC; equal-millisecond and backward/future-dated-predecessor cases refuse without committing the new WKO/registry state. The diagnostic must expose predecessor_map_filename, predecessor_utc, and observed_host_utc. A separate fixture must deliberately move the future-dated current WKO MAP out of the active Suitcase, rescan, and prove deterministic reselection of the remaining current structurally valid WKO MAP without Data Sculptor silently moving or deleting anything itself. Day 060 H-12: every equal/backward/future-predecessor chronology refusal in this acceptance set must emit DS-UTC-001 with exact map_profile: WKO, observed_host_utc, predecessor_map_filename, and predecessor_utc facts.

F-23 save-transaction filesystem-fault fixture, reconciled by F-33: using a controlled create/write/close/rename/promotion failure at a deterministic point after a valid WIP has entered the governed save path, acceptance must prove that a failed WKO/WKO-MAP save is never represented as a committed alias-registry update. The pre-run current WKO MAP must remain authoritative; no malformed or unpromoted candidate may become current; and any rollback or retained SCR evidence must follow W002-STOR-018.3 and the shared non-Store publication/retained-evidence contract. No RCV artifact is emitted.

F-02 registry-repair acceptance set

  • Deadlock escape: with a repair-required current WKO MAP, a newly saved structurally valid repair-only WKO can Run by exact filename and successfully publish a repaired successor registry.
  • No broad bypass: a newly saved unregistered WKO for any other operation remains ineligible to Run.
  • Missing reference: repair removes a stale registry row but does not recreate the missing WKO, substitute a historical WKO, or promote an older WKO automatically.
  • Discovered alias, no owner: one discovered valid WKO with an otherwise unowned alias becomes CURRENT.
  • Discovered alias collision: a discovered WKO whose alias is already owned by a surviving CURRENT row becomes DEPRECATED.
  • Several discovered WKOs, no owner: all become DEPRECATED; no winner is inferred by UTC, filename, UUID, directory order, discovery order, or modified time.
  • Mandatory alias: an unaliased WKO cannot be structurally valid.
  • Line endings: otherwise-identical structurally valid WKO fixtures with LF and CRLF line endings are accepted; the lone-CR form refuses.
  • Deterministic successor: repaired successor rows serialize in ascending UTF-8 byte order of exact wko_filename.
  • Historical Run: a registered DEPRECATED WKO can Run by exact physical filename but not by alias.
  • Receipt identity: a successful or refused registry-repair Receipt uses REPAIR_WORK_ORDER_REGISTRY as the operation token.

Day 060 H-10 / BM-07 registry-repair Receipt-count acceptance

Acceptance must include a successful repair-required-registry fixture in which the exact repair-only bootstrap WKO is initially visible and unregistered, runs by the bounded exact-filename bootstrap, and is then registered by the repair result.

  • The committed successor WKO MAP must contain the repair WKO row.
  • The successful Receipt must list that exact repair WKO under either REGISTERED_CURRENT_WKO_<INDEX>_FILENAME or REGISTERED_DEPRECATED_WKO_<INDEX>_FILENAME, according to the ordinary alias-ownership rule.
  • The corresponding REGISTERED_*_COUNT must equal the number of newly registered rows in that status class, including the repair WKO when applicable.
  • Pre-existing surviving CURRENT/DEPRECATED rows in the base registry must not inflate either registered count.
  • A fixture containing both pre-existing surviving rows and newly registered rows must prove that the Receipt reports the repair change set while the successor MAP reports the complete resulting registry state.
W002-WKO-ACC-005

Store MAP inheritance, historical override, and immutable snapshot acceptance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

An acceptance fixture must execute a saved Store-establishing Work Order containing multiple COL alias assignments when no routable Store lineage exists and no structurally malformed Store-MAP-class artifact is present, and prove that exactly one new immutable complete Store MAP is created while the GUI supplies no alias-edit gesture and target artifacts remain unchanged.

A later Work Order with the same exact source and no explicit MAP must route to that Store's lineage and inherit its unique newest permitted MAP automatically. Another Work Order must explicitly select an older valid MAP even though newer MAPs for that Store exist and prove that Store/RID binding, alias resolution, and inheritance use exactly the named historical MAP instead. A fixture specifying more than one MAP must refuse. A fixture with two otherwise permitted current MAP candidates for the selected Store sharing the greatest UTC millisecond timestamp must refuse automatic inheritance rather than use UUID as chronology.

A separate fixture must remove or corrupt every Store MAP in a prior lineage so that no structurally valid Store MAP remains while at least one malformed Store-MAP-class artifact remains visible in the active Suitcase. Re-running ordinary materialization must refuse before creating a new RID or first Store MAP, and Help must identify the malformed MAP artifact or artifacts.

P2-03 Store chronology acceptance: injected-clock fixtures must prove later observed UTC success, equal-millisecond refusal, backward-UTC refusal, and a genuinely future-dated current Store MAP that remains current while blocking successor publication. Every refusal must leave the chronology predecessor unchanged and publish no successor Store MAP. A historical-base fixture must derive requested state from an older eligible MAP while proving that the strict-greater-than comparison uses the actual current Store MAP as chronology predecessor, not the historical base. A deliberate analyst-removal fixture must move the future-dated current MAP out of the active Suitcase and prove deterministic reselection of the remaining structurally valid history; restoring that MAP must make ordinary greatest-UTC authority rules applicable again. Day 060 H-12: every equal/backward/future-predecessor Store-MAP chronology refusal in this acceptance set must emit DS-UTC-001 with exact map_profile: STORE, observed_host_utc, predecessor_map_filename, and predecessor_utc facts.

W002-WKO-ACC-006

Work Order chaining refusal acceptance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

An acceptance fixture must submit a structurally saved WKO containing a RUN or other recognized Work Order-invocation construct and prove that WASM-002 refuses it during validation before Stage 1, Stage 2, conversion, inventory, or other governed execution begins.

The diagnostic/Help output must identify composition as deferred functionality. A separate multi-column MATERIALIZE fixture must still succeed, proving that multiple selected columns inside one Work Order are not misclassified as Work Order chaining.

W002-UI-001

One explicit Work Order command surface

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The WASM-002 browser front end shall use the Work Order editor as the single human command-entry surface for governed execution. It shall not expose a second interactive command prompt or point-and-click analytical path that can become an independent source of analytical intent.

The editable draft may be syntax-highlighted, validated, and saved, but it is not itself executable authority. The browser Run action operates only on one loaded/selected saved immutable WKO that is eligible under the governed Work Order registry rules. Run is a browser action, not a line that ordinary WASM-002 Work Orders must contain.

If a WKO contains the reserved DS-STEPS RUN composition token, WASM-002 refuses before executing any child or top-level analytical operation because saved-Work-Order chaining is deferred. The token remains reserved so later ordered composition can be added without repurposing existing syntax.

F-24 fresh-application state: each new Data Sculptor browser application instance begins without a selected Suitcase and without a restored unsaved Work Order draft. Initial page load and full reload therefore return the command surface to the pre-Suitcase gate. A previously selected folder, loaded WKO, or dirty WIP must not be silently reconstructed from browser-private persistence.

W002-UI-002

Front end presents and authorizes; shared Rust core decides

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The browser front end may authorize files, edit and validate Work Orders, invoke the shared engine, display governed state, render diagnostics, and present generated artifacts. It must not independently decide analytical truth, silently reinterpret a Work Order, or implement a competing semantic path.

Where front-end presentation and shared-core semantics disagree, the shared governed semantics and frozen requirements are authoritative.

W002-UI-003

Visible Suitcase and governed run context

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The WASM-002 browser surface shall make the currently validated Suitcase visible and shall expose the visible files in that folder. Source and requested-column context become governed execution state only when a saved Work Order resolves them; the UI must not imply that directory presence alone means a source has been selected, scanned, certified, or materialized.

W002-UI-004

Certification gate is visible and blocking

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The front end shall visibly represent strict whole-file UTF-8 certification as a required stage before analytical materialization. A certification refusal must stop the current analytical Work Order, prevent later materialization stages from being presented as successful, and provide the canonical diagnostic / Help path.

W002-UI-005

One-pass multi-column materialization is represented truthfully

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

When a valid Work Order requests multiple source columns, the front end shall represent them as one governed multi-column materialization request through one bounded structural CSV pass, not as unrelated per-column scans when the frozen engine contract performs one pass.

Requested columns must be validated before data-row materialization begins, consistent with the materialization requirements.

W002-UI-006

Visible Suitcase Directory is the artifact orientation surface

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

After Suitcase validation, the browser shall present a human-readable directory view of the visible files in the selected Suitcase, including physical filename, read-only governed alias where applicable, file type, and size. Governed artifacts created by a run shall appear in that same visible inventory after refresh or update.

The directory is an orientation and metadata surface over the real flat Suitcase. It is not a hidden browser cache, a second persistence system, or an analytical command surface.

CAT integration: this existing directory remains the sole WASM-002 artifact-orientation surface. CAT and MAP artifacts are first-ranked under W002-CAT-UI-001 through W002-CAT-UI-008; no second catalog browser is introduced.

W002-UI-007

All user-facing Help flows through the Help Engine

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

All Data Sculptor-controlled user-facing Help messages, warnings, refusals, explanations, validation guidance, safe-next-action messages, and governed success/status messages that participate in the Help/status/evidence system shall be produced through the Help Engine from governed facts or canonical diagnostic events. Individual UI controls must not maintain an independent competing stock of semantic Help text.

Governed success/status events in this system use canonical INFO diagnostics. Ordinary static labels, headings, decorative copy, and presentation-only UI text are not diagnostics and need not be routed through the diagnostic registry merely because they are visible.

Help voice may change wording and depth but must not change diagnostic identity, evidence, severity, refusal/continue behavior, provenance, or safe next action. Durable Help Reports derive from the same governed truth.

F-17 fallback behavior: when a complete registered diagnostic lacks an authored help_messages.json entry, the UI must show the deterministic Generic Technical Help rendering from W002-HELP-002.9 for Casual, Office Speak, and Technical selections rather than a blank state, guessed prose, or UI-local explanation. When diagnostic assembly itself fails its required-fact contract, the UI presents DS-HLP-001; it must not display the incomplete intended diagnostic as if valid.

W002-UI-008

Legacy encoding conversion remains a separate operation

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

If UTF-8 certification fails and the bytes are eligible for the separately governed Windows-1252 compatibility/conversion path, the front end may explain or help draft that separate conversion Work Order. It must not silently reinterpret the failed analytical Work Order as Windows-1252 and continue materialization.

P3-08 front-end disclosure: after a successful conversion, the visible result/Help path must identify the exact published CVT filename and explain that it is a new source identity for later Store routing. When that CVT is subsequently chosen for first materialization, the front end must not present the action as a refresh of an earlier conversion-derived Store merely because the analyst-owned input filename is the same; it must preserve the governed Help disclosure that each distinct CVT is a distinct source artifact and lineage input.

W002-UI-009

Front-end branding is presentation-only

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The WASM-002 browser front end shall use the canonical built-in Red5Sorcery/Data Sculptor branding and approved presentation tokens without changing analytical or diagnostic meaning. The current Red5Sorcery identity treatment, including the red “5”, remains the active WASM-002 design direction.

Configurable Brand Manifest loading, validation, selection, and substitution are deferred to V1-BACKLOG / a future build whose number is not yet assigned.

W002-UI-010

WASM-002 front end must not preview deferred analytical features as available controls

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The WASM-002 front end shall stop at the capabilities allocated to the WASM-002 build slice. It shall not present filtering, grouping, sorting, Quick Viz, PRETTY Tables, DS-VERIFY, or later filter-driven build/export workflows as executable WASM-002 controls unless their individual requirement SCOPE is deliberately changed and frozen.

W002-PLAT-001

WASM-002/V1 browser and modest-hardware acceptance baseline

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The canonical modest-hardware acceptance machine for the WASM-002 browser release and the browser path carried into V1 is the project's 11-inch Windows 11 laptop with an Intel N100 processor, 16 GB RAM, and a 1920×1200 native display. Each acceptance record must capture the exact tested Windows build, browser version, Windows display scaling, browser zoom, and materially relevant machine configuration. Those observed version and presentation settings are acceptance evidence; they do not become timeless minimum-version requirements unless separately frozen.

V1 browser support is scoped to certified desktop Chromium hosts that expose the user-selected writable-directory and file-publication capabilities required by the visible Suitcase contract. Microsoft Edge is the primary certified browser. Google Chrome is the secondary certified browser. Another Chromium-derived browser may work, but Data Sculptor must not claim it as a certified V1 browser until that browser has passed the applicable acceptance suite. Firefox and Safari are not supported V1 browser hosts under this contract and their lack of the required filesystem capability must not block V1 release.

Supported-host acceptance must exercise the real browser filesystem path: explicit user-selected Suitcase access, CER validation, governed Work Order save/Run behavior, and governed artifact publication. Data Sculptor must not substitute OPFS, IndexedDB, download-only publication, a browser extension, or another hidden/different persistence model merely to make an unsupported browser appear supported.

Required filesystem capability is feature-detected before folder validation begins. If the host cannot expose the governed writable-directory contract, Data Sculptor must treat that state as a host-capability refusal, keep governed save/Run/analytical controls locked, and route the explanation through the canonical diagnostic/Help path. It must not claim that a particular user folder failed validation when no folder could actually be tested.

W002-UI-011

Keyboard-operable, small-screen browser shell

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The required WASM-002 front-end interactions shall remain operable from a keyboard and usable on the canonical modest-hardware/small-screen baseline defined by W002-PLAT-001. At the display scaling and browser zoom recorded for acceptance, every required control and governed surface needed to complete the supported workflow must remain reachable without changing those settings merely to reveal an otherwise inaccessible control.

Responsive reflow and ordinary scrolling are permitted; this requirement does not demand that every panel be visible simultaneously. Visible labels must carry meaning without relying on color alone. Exact shortcut assignments are presentation details unless separately frozen.

W002-UI-012

Reference prototype is evidence, not a shadow specification

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The Day 043 HTML prototype embedded below is retained as concrete design evidence for the WASM-002 browser workbench. Its layout, simulated analytical execution, illustrative Work Order grammar, current aliases, demo shortcuts, artifact examples, and other unfrozen literals do not become normative merely because they appear in the prototype.

If the embedded prototype conflicts with a numbered requirement, the numbered requirement governs and the prototype must be revised.

W002-UI-013

Dedicated persistent Help / Diagnostic Surface

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The primary WASM-002 workspace must reserve a dedicated Help / Diagnostic Surface with stable layout presence. When a governed diagnostic is active, the analyst must be able to view its explanation without losing sight of the Work Order and the execution/source context required to understand it.

The persistent surface is a viewport into canonical diagnostic truth; it is not a second state authority.

W002-UI-014

Governed analytical refusals are not modal- or toast-only interactions

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

An application-controlled modal dialog must not be the primary presentation of a governed analytical refusal when it would obscure the Work Order or execution context. A transient toast or timed notification must not be the sole carrier of governed diagnostic truth.

Browser- or operating-system-controlled permission/security dialogs are outside this requirement because Data Sculptor does not control their presentation.

W002-UI-015

Idle Help state remains semantically quiet

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

When no canonical diagnostic is active, the Help / Diagnostic Surface should communicate only restrained readiness/idle state rather than becoming a general dashboard for unrelated metrics, checkpoints, or project status. Exact wording such as “No active diagnostic. Ready.” is presentation detail unless separately frozen.

W002-UI-016

Help surface exposes a direct saved-report action

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

From an active governed diagnostic, including a non-run diagnostic, or from one governed Run whose diagnostic history is available to the Help surface, the browser Help / Diagnostic Surface must provide an explicit action to generate the durable HTML Help Report. Each explicit report request publishes exactly one HLP under W002-HELP-003.2 and W002-HELP-009.

The generated report must become a visible Suitcase artifact governed by the Help, PRETTY, persistence, and provenance requirements and must use the canonical built-in Data Sculptor presentation.

W002-UI-017

Writable Suitcase validation is the first interaction gate

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Before Data Sculptor enables Work Order saving, governed Run, or analytical processing, the analyst must choose one Suitcase folder and Data Sculptor must validate that folder by successfully creating, completely writing, and closing one governed HTML Suitcase Validation Certificate under W002-STOR-022 through W002-STOR-022.3. Permission state or directory enumeration alone is not sufficient to pass the gate.

The successful certificate remains visibly in the Suitcase as durable evidence. Validation does not require deleting or renaming the certificate. Until the certificate write/close succeeds, the analytical workspace remains locked except for Help and Suitcase selection.

Browser- or operating-system-controlled refusal of protected directories is outside Data Sculptor presentation control and must be explained through the Help Engine when the host can observe the refusal.

F-24 opening/selection lifecycle: merely loading Data Sculptor does not create a CER. A CER is published only after an explicit Suitcase selection successfully passes the governed validation gate. Reselecting and successfully validating the same physical Suitcase is a new certification event and publishes one new CER; all earlier CERs remain untouched. Data Sculptor does not remember the directory handle between application instances, so a new load/reload requires explicit Suitcase selection again before the workspace can unlock.

W002-UI-018

Suitcase Directory enumerates visible files before analytical work

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Immediately after Suitcase validation, Data Sculptor shall enumerate the visible files available through the authorized directory handle and show them in the Suitcase Directory. No source, header, column, certification, or materialization state shall be inferred merely from the existence of those files.

W002-UI-019

Directory inventory and displayed aliases must not become point-and-click analytical intent

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The Suitcase Directory may expose file inventory and read-only human-facing metadata such as aliases, but it shall not provide alias-edit controls, “Use as source,” column-pick, materialize, filter, or equivalent governed-action controls.

Source files, requested columns, alias mutations, and analytical operations are stated in saved Work Orders and resolved by the governed engine.

W002-UI-020

Saved Work Orders are the only Run targets

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The Work Order editor may create a new draft or load a saved Work Order TXT artifact from the validated Suitcase. A loaded saved Work Order is an immutable Run target and may be inspected or run directly. If the analyst changes its instruction text, the editor must transition to a new draft derived from that saved Work Order; the draft is not runnable until it is saved as a new immutable Work Order with a new governed physical identity. The original saved Work Order remains unchanged.

W002-UI-021

User chooses the Suitcase; Data Sculptor chooses generated filenames

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

For Work Orders, materialized columns, Help Reports, receipts, maps, and other Data Sculptor-generated artifacts, the analyst chooses or has already chosen the validated Suitcase folder. The browser shall not require the analyst to supply an output filename for those governed artifacts.

W002-UI-022

Execution Output is read-only observation, never command input

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The browser shall provide a read-only Execution Output surface that reports which saved Work Order was run, how its source and governed aliases resolved, which execution stages occurred, what was refused, and which governed artifacts were created or assigned. For WASM-002 it does not display a nested Work Order invocation chain because Work Order composition is deferred.

The surface shall not accept commands, analytical text, or cursor-driven execution input.

W002-UI-023

The browser has no separate Work Order Description field

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The browser must not expose a standalone editable Description field for a saved or draft Work Order. Human-facing Work Order naming is authored in DS-STEPS with the required WORK ORDER AS "..." clause inside the Work Order itself.

The Saved Work Order chooser and Suitcase Directory may display governed WKO alias/lifecycle information from the current structurally valid WKO MAP. Where lifecycle information is shown, CURRENT and DEPRECATED are read-only governed registry state, and the exact physical WKO filename must remain available/visible so human meaning, lifecycle authority, and physical identity remain distinct. Alias resolution uses the sole CURRENT row for the exact alias; a DEPRECATED row is historical evidence rather than the alias target.

If that current registry references a missing physical WKO, the MAP remains current and the registry is repair-required; the browser must not silently display an older WKO MAP as though it had become current merely because of the missing reference. A structurally malformed newer WKO MAP never becomes current and is reported through Help/evidence surfaces.

Editing a loaded saved WKO—including changing its alias or comments—creates a derived draft that must be saved as a new immutable WKO before it can Run. If that save would supersede the existing CURRENT target for the same alias, the save flow follows the exact Replace alias target / Cancel decision in W002-STOR-018.3; the UI must not provide a separate direct registry-edit gesture.

W002-UI-024

Suitcase Directory aliases are read-only views of governed MAP profiles

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

Alias displays in the Suitcase Directory are observation-only. Store, RID, and materialized-COL aliases are read from eligible Store MAP state. Saved Work Order alias and lifecycle state are read from the current structurally valid WKO MAP. The browser may aggregate those governed sources into one human-facing directory view while keeping exact physical filenames available for inspection.

For WKO rows, CURRENT/DEPRECATED is read-only governed lifecycle metadata. A CURRENT row identifies the registry target for that exact alias; a DEPRECATED row remains historical registry evidence and must not be presented as the current alias target.

The GUI must not expose an input, inline editor, context action, or other non-Work-Order path that directly mutates governed aliases or WKO lifecycle status. Store/RID/COL alias mutation remains Work-Order-governed. WKO aliases are authored inside immutable WKO text with WORK ORDER AS and enter or change WKO alias-registry authority only through a successful governed save transaction under W002-STOR-018.3.

W002-UI-025

The browser has exactly two governed built-in presentation themes

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The WASM-002 browser presentation contract exposes exactly two governed theme choices: Modern Dark and Modern Light. Custom presentation is deferred to V1-BACKLOG / a future build not yet numbered. A Terminal theme is not part of the WASM-002/V1 browser contract and must not be exposed as a governed theme choice.

Theme selection is presentation-only. It must not change Work Order semantics, source resolution, diagnostic identity or facts, continue/refuse decisions, analytical values, Receipt truth, or other governed execution meaning.

The selected browser theme does not control durable HLP or CER presentation in WASM-002. Those governed HTML artifacts use the canonical built-in Red5Sorcery/Data Sculptor presentation regardless of whether the live browser is using Modern Dark or Modern Light.

F-24 session default and persistence: Modern Dark is the canonical theme at the start of every new browser application instance. The analyst may switch to Modern Light during that instance, but WASM-002 retains the choice only in volatile runtime state and does not persist it in browser-private storage. A new application instance therefore returns to Modern Dark.

W002-UI-026

Flight Recorder is a read-only derived Receipt-history surface

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The WASM-002 browser may present a Flight Recorder surface that is derived exclusively from governed RCP Receipt artifacts currently visible in the authorized Suitcase. The surface is read-only and regenerable. It must not create or maintain a second execution-history database, mutable log, hidden cache, browser-private history, or alternate chronology authority.

The Flight Recorder may sort, filter, group, or summarize Receipt-derived facts for human orientation, but those presentation operations must not alter Receipt bytes, invent missing events, or become authoritative over the underlying immutable Receipts. Where no canonical Receipt exists because Receipt publication failed, the surface must not reconstruct a substitute original Receipt from UI state, console text, or memory.

W002-UI-ACC-001

Single-command-surface and saved-run-target acceptance

UNDER REVIEW
SCOPEWASM-002BUILD—

The acceptance check must show one Work Order editor that can hold either a new draft or a loaded saved Work Order and no second independent prompt, command-entry cursor, point-and-click source selector, or point-and-click column selector.

A governed browser Run must read exactly one loaded/selected saved immutable WKO artifact that is eligible under the current registry rules. An unsaved WIP must not Run. Editing the instruction text of a loaded saved WKO must transition the editor to a new draft state that cannot Run until saved as a new immutable WKO.
